News.title: Moment flip flop-wearing ‘dine & dasher’ sprints out city centre Chinese restaurant without paying as waiters chase him
News.content:
THIS is the moment a man in flip flops flees a family run Chinese restaurant without paying his bill, as waiters chase him down the street.

Noodle Alley in Manchester released CCTV footage of the brazen diner after he ditched his table on Tuesday.



Clad in black shorts, a black button up shirt and flip flops the customer can be seen standing up from his table and making his way to the door.

He confidently waves at a waitress before making his way out of the restaurant.



Noticing that he hasn’t paid, a member of staff drops a tray of dishes in her hands and gives chase.

The man notices he is being followed and bolts up a flight of stairs towards the street.

Video from outside the shop shows him charging off down the street, desperate to shake off his pursuers.

Seconds later the waitress emerges from the restaurant but gives up the chase as the man makes his way across the road.



The restaurant, on Faulkner Street, shared the footage with the caption: “Today, someone ran away from our restaurant without paying.

“This isn’t just about the money.

“Small independent businesses are already struggling with rising costs, and dealing with people who deliberately run away without paying makes it even harder.

“Every meal, every member of staff, and every genuine customer matters.

“Our team reacted immediately and tried to catch him, but he disappeared within seconds.



“We have a very clear CCTV image of the individual, and all the evidence has been passed to the relevant authorities.

“To everyone who chooses to support small independent businesses like ours, thank you.

“Your kindness and support help keep businesses like ours going.”

A member of staff told the Manchester Evening News: “I went to get some chicken legs for the restaurant and when I came back the staff told me one guy got up and ran out.

“So I went to look at the CCTV. He stayed a very short time. He came in, only had noodles and he sat in a booth, actually looking around the bar, waiting for a moment that he could run.



“He saw a family go up to pay and he probably thought it was the best moment.

“A member of staff got up after him to clean the table and then realised he hadn’t paid, so they chased him, but as soon as he got up the stairs he was running so fast, he was already off down the road.”

They added: “I know it’s not a lot of money, but it is hurtful. The effort we put in hoping for everybody to enjoy their meal and then we are being let down.

“This is not the first time it’s happened to us. We opened about three years ago and we’ve had other guests leave without paying.

“We are not like a fast food restaurant, we work very hard and it’s very competitive. I sacrifice my evenings to be at home with my daughter just to make sure we can do our business.



“It makes me sad, because Manchester is such a special place and most people here are very nice.

“I’ve lived in Manchester 26 years now. I came when I was doing university so I decided this was the perfect city. You don’t want things like this to ruin that, or the reputation of Manchester.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We could chase them, but it’s not worth the risk. You don’t know what’s going to happen next time, it could be dangerous. [Staff] did make the effort but he was really fast.”

Noodle Alley reported the incident to the Greater Manchester Police who have since confirmed they are investigating reports of a theft.

News.title: German airport worker KICKED ‘military-grade bomb carried by Russian drone to blow up jet loaded with ammo for Ukraine’
News.content:
A GERMAN airport worker stopped a potential disaster by booting a suspected Russian drone carrying a military-grade bomb out of the air.

The explosive-laden UAV was spotted over Leipzig airport and flew worryingly close to a fleet of Ukrainian aircraft loaded up with ammo.



Investigators have now revealed the drone was first seen by the south runway at the Leipzig/Halle Airport on August 4 at around 11.42pm.

It was hovering between two Ukrainian An-124 cargo planes which led to the workers rushing to try and bring it down.



One employee managed to get close enough so he could bravely kick the drone as it was flying near him, according to DPA, Germany‘s largest news agency.

Police deployed a bomb disposal robot to inspect the stricken drone and found it had been equipped with professional explosives and a detonator.

Germany’s Interior Minister, Alexander Dobrindt, praised the airport worker but said the drone crashing down to the ground could have had serious consequences.

He said a “ripped” detonator on the explosive package was the only thing that prevented the device from going off as it hit the tarmac.



If it had exploded then the blast could have not only injured those nearby but also set light to the aircraft, its fuel and the ammo inside.

Dobrindt said the drone’s explosive cargo points towards it being a failed hybrid attack potentially from “foreign powers”.

The close call came just before a landing plane struck a mystery flying object at the same airport in another major security alert.

Germany’s federal prosecutor has taken on the investigation, along with Nato representatives, into the suspected drone attack.

The Office of the Federal Prosecutor said the “serious attack likely targeted Germany’s transport and logistics infrastructure.”



The airport in Leipzig is the main base for Nato’s Strategic Airlift International Solution.

Putin ‘is prepared to take down a passenger jet in Europe’ THE explosive-laden drone found at a German airport shows Vladimir Putin is prepared to take down a European passenger jet, an expert has warned. Security expert Will Geddes said the terrifying breaches had “shaken fear across not only militaries and across the world, but also commercial airports”. And he warned the chilling ordeal proved that Putin is more than capable of using a drone to blow up a passenger plane in Europe. Geddes told The Sun: “It’s a disaster waiting to happen.” He added that the device could have been adapted to carry radioactive material or even a biological weapon. Geddes said: “The visible demonstration of the ability to get close to a cargo plane in an airport in Leipzig shows that if that had detonated… that would have had a drastic impact.” He also warned the West was lacking in the necessary countermeasures to defend against drones – a weakpoint which could leave Britain vulnerable. Read more here…

It is one of the main European hubs for delivering equipment to strengthen Nato’s eastern flank using a small fleet of Antonov cargo planes.

As opposition Green Party spokesman Konstantin von Notz said: “Should it transpire that a state is behind this action, this would constitute state terrorism directed against Germany and its citizens.”

German officials are yet to identify any suspects but several security experts and European ambassadors say it bears all the hallmarks of the Kremlin.



Kyiv’s ambassador to Germany Oleksii Makeiev said: “Who else could it be but Russia?“

Security expert Will Geddes told The Sun Putin is more than capable of using a drone to blow up a passenger plane in Europe.

Russia has already proved it is capable of taking down passenger jets in Europe.

In 2014, Malaysia Airlines flight MH17 was shot down with a Russian-made missile over eastern Ukraine, killing all 298 people on board.

Moscow was found responsible for the disaster which took place over the Donbas region while pro-Russian rebels were fighting Ukrainians.



European security agencies have been probing a series of incendiary devices concealed in parcels that caught fire in 2024.

Main suspect Vladimir Putin has been frequently accused of planting a parcel bomb on a flight headed to a depot in the UK.

Russia has denied any involvement in the 2024 incidents and the more recent overflights.

News.title: New hosepipe ban comes into force for 1.8MILLION people tomorrow with more areas affected
News.content:
A NEW hosepipe ban is set to come into force for around 1.8million Brits tomorrow, as vast parts of the country continue to face restrictions.

Half of England and the entirety of Wales are still battling drought conditions as a result of prolonged dry weather.

South West Water has announced a hosepipe ban from the early hours of tomorrow (August 8), with most of the south-West of England set to be impacted.



All customers across Devon, Cornwall, parts of Dorset, Somerset, and the Isles of Scilly will be affected as a result of prolonged dry weather.



Restrictions will come into force from 0.01am tomorrow, but customers have been urged to follow restrictions immediately to reserve water supplies.

There is already an active ban by South West Water across Mid Devon and parts of East Devon, but the new restrictions will impact even more customers.

Sam Bottomley, of South West Water said “exceptionally low rainfall” and “high demand during warmer weather” had provoked the decision to introduce restriction, alongside the ongoing drought status.

He continued: “Introducing a hosepipe ban is never a decision we take lightly, and we fully appreciate the inconvenience it will cause.

Full list of regions affected by South West Water's new hosepipe ban The restrictions will be enforced from 0.01am on Saturday, August 8 Devon

Cornwall

Parts of Dorset

Parts of Somerset

The Isles of Scilly

“However, these temporary restrictions are an important step in helping to protect our rivers and essential water supplies for homes, businesses and critical services across the region.”

South West Water has urged customers to use water resourcefully by taking shorter showers, turning off taps when brushing teeth, and only running washing machines and dishwashers with full loads.



Under a temporary use ban, customers cannot use a hosepipe, sprinkler, or pressure washer for various activities, such as watering plants or filling up hot tubs.

Anyone caught breaking these rules can face a £1,000 fine, unless an approved exemption or loophole is in place.

Drought conditions continue to impact half of England and the entirety of Wales, with nine water companies introducing bans for over 23million customers in recent months.

If your water supplier is affected, it is important to check their website to find out if your postcode has been impacted by temporary use bans.

News.title: Afghan ‘suitcase killer’ suspect ‘had issues’ with authority and would ‘feel sorry for himself’, adoptive family reveals
News.content:
THE Afghan boxer accused of killing a Brit woman in Athens had “issues with authority”, according to his “adoptive” parents.

An American couple who took in Sharif Ahmadzai, 26, a decade ago revealed the murder suspect would often feel “sorry for himself” during his rebellious teen years.



They shared their disbelief at the heinous crime Ahmadzai is accused of and the callous manner in which he stuffed the body of Elisabeth Ross in a suitcase before discarding it in a derelict building.

Ross, 38, a Scottish Christian missionary who was living in Athens volunteering for a charity was found on July 18 – just three days after she first went missing.



The US nationals told the Daily Mail they are heartbroken to learn of the alleged crimes of the teenager who had lived with them for almost two years.

The adoptive father said: “He had issues like everybody else does. There could be some trying times with him, but it was usually more rebellion against authority or just him feeling sorry for himself.”



He said the Ahmadzai he knew is not the same person today.

The couple say the accused murderer never showed any signs that he was capable of such brutal violence however did admit he had issues.



His wife mentioned that he would “act out” – though no more than a typical teenager – and noted that, like many refugees, Ahmadzai experienced “much trauma”.

The couple took in the Afghan boxer while undertaking humanitarian aid work at the Moria refugee camp in 2016 and the trio became so close Ahmadzai called the couple mom and dad.

He lived with the couple for two years until they returned to their home in Atlanta, Georgia, and they last saw him in 2019.



Ahmadzai’s adoptive mother reportedly sobbed upon hearing the charges saying it doesn’t feel real.

She said: “When I heard the news, I couldn’t imagine it to be true. Not in a million years.

“I keep thinking I’m gonna wake up and it was a nightmare, and it’s over.



“It’s a heartbreak that you can’t understand. It’s like I have the heart of a mother for that now adult-sized boy.”

Ahmadzai’s life story was previously told in an autobiographical animated video – and soon in an upcoming memoir – From Hell to Home: How Loss, Exile, and Hope Built the Man I Became.

He shared how his entire family were wiped out in Afghanistan.

He fled Kabul in 2016, embarking on a 45-day trek through Pakistan, Iran, and Turkey.



He survived two failed boat crossings before finally reaching Lesvos, Greece, and entering Moria Camp where he met the American couple.

Ahmadzai met his future wife American Christian missionary Alaina Hall, 28, who was volunteering with a relief charity in the camp.

The couple married in 2023 and set up a refugee charity together – where they are believed to have met another fellow Christian, Elisabeth Ross.

Ahmadzai’s wife allegedly reported her husband to cops after she became suspicious he was involved in Elisabeth’s death.



The brave wife gave a testimony after she became concerned about her husband’s actions.

Alaina last saw Scottish charity worker Elisabeth on July 12, leaving her alone with her husband, Ahmadzai.

Elisabeth was killed three days later, on July 15.

That night, Alaina woke up to find Ahmadzai gone.

Tracking his phone, she located him at Elisabeth’s apartment building.



He claimed he was just using her bathroom while he was out watching football.

When news broke of a body found in a nearby suitcase, Alaina suspected the victim was Elisabeth and her husband was the killer.

Alaina remembers Elisabeth as “a very pleasant and sweet person, kind-hearted, with a good soul”.

Ahmadzai denies murdering Elisabeth.

He exercised his right to silence at a Greek court on Thursday and did not respond ​to the charges, awaiting other evidence, his lawyer said.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The court ordered him to be held in jail pending trial.

The suspect has already admitted to putting Elisabeth’s body into a suitcase and taking her to the abandoned site.

News.title: Brit mum, 45, admits smuggling £500,000-worth of cannabis into UK after bragging she was ‘heading home to cut the grass’
News.content:
DRUG BUST MUM Brit mum, 45, admits smuggling £500,000-worth of cannabis into UK after bragging she was ‘heading home to cut the grass’

A BRIT mum has admitted smuggling over £500,000 worth of cannabis into the UK inside her suitcases.

Amy Jayne Durban stuffed her luggage full of 51.2kg of the illegal substance on a flight back home from Thailand.



The 45-year-old’s haul had a street value of around £512,000.

Durban, from Hemyock, Cullompton, Devon, was greeted by border force after arriving back in the UK on July 6.



She was the centre of a National Crime Agency investigation and was arrested in Heathrow Airport after jetting in from Bangkok.

After appearing at Uxbridge Magistrates’ Court in July, she pleaded guilty to smuggling Class B drugs at Isleworth Crown Court on Thursday.



She was remanded into custody and her sentencing is due to take place on October 14.

Just days before her arrest, Amy made a cryptic post on social media.

She said on Facebook: “On her way home to cut the grass if you know what I mean. No ETA so you won’t know I’m about to hit your lawn.”

According to the NCA, there has been a rapid rise in drug couriers attempting to smuggle cannabis into the UK.



Brits are usually approached on social media by organised gangs who are offering a “free” holiday and spending money in exchange for being smugglers.

They are tasked with taking the cannabis home where other criminals in the UK will pick them up and move them on.

A jaw-dropping 464 per cent increase in cannabis plane smugglers was seen between 2023 and 2024 – jumping from 142 to 801 people being caught.



The figure rose once again in 2025 and 2026 is reportedly on track to be even worse – with 600 passengers arrested in the first six months of the year.



Durban’s conviction comes after NCA and partners in Thailand announced a new crackdown in the country.

Those caught trying to smuggle cannabis now face huge fines, equating to £680 per kilogram.

An “average” smuggler is caught in Thailand with 26kg – which would land them with a £17,680 fine.

If not paid, the smuggler faces a two-year jail sentence in a Thai prison.

Mark Abbott, NCA senior investigating officer, said: “There are really bad outcomes at home and abroad when couriers are caught smuggling cannabis.



“As well as time in prison, a life-changing conviction will damage future career and travel prospects.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“People should understand that these crime groups use profits from cannabis smuggling to fund the trafficking of other drugs too.

“All of those drugs fuel wider crime in our communities and have a toxic effect on people’s lives.”

News.title: Young man ‘sexually assaulted by group of masked men’ in road near leisure park as cops launch urgent hunt
News.content:
HORROR ATTACK Young man ‘sexually assaulted by group of masked men’ in road near leisure park as cops launch urgent hunt

COPS have launched a probe after a young man was allegedly sexually assaulted by a group of masked men near a leisure park.

The victim was reportedly targeted in Nuneaton, Warwickshire, in the early hours of Wednesday.



The three men – all said to be wearing black clothing, masks and gloves – reportedly attacked the young man at around 1am.

Cops have cordoned off a large stretch of road near Bermuda Leisure Park after the assault allegedly occurred on a nearby bridge over the A444.



One of the attackers was described as being around 5ft 10in tall and of large build, according to Warwickshire Police.

The second man was slim and around 6ft 2in, while the third was around 5ft 8in tall and of medium build, the force added.



It is believed one was wearing black and white trainers, possibly Nike Air Force 1s, while another was described as having blue eyes.

Inspector Ryan Walker said: “We know our residents will be concerned by this attack, and the victim is being supported by specialist officers.

“Within minutes of this attack first being reported, an urgent investigation was launched, with a cordon in place today.

“Our neighbourhood officers will be out and about in the area. Please come talk to them if you have any concerns.”



Issuing a statement, Warwickshire Police urged anyone with information on the attack to come forward.

It read: “We are continuing to investigate this attack, and specialist officers are supporting the victim.

“We would also like to take this chance to remind everyone that when someone has been through such a traumatic event, they may struggle to give detailed descriptions of suspects.

“It is a normal response to severe trauma. When leaving comments that are critical of that description, we would ask that people consider the impact that those comments might have should victims see them.

“Our detectives are working around the clock to identify the three men, and our local policing team remain in the area.



“Please come and talk to them if you have any concerns or information that could help our investigation.

“If you were in the area at the time of the attack or you have information, you can also call 101, giving incident number 53 of August 5.”

News.title: Horror as car stolen with toddler still inside in UK city with cops hunting down thief
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CHILD TAKEN Horror as car stolen with toddler still inside in UK city with cops hunting down thief

A CAR with a two-year-old child inside has been stolen before later being abandoned and recovered, as cops hunt down the thief.

The grey Volvo was nicked from Long Thorpe Lane in Wakefield, West Yorkshire, at around 8.30pm on Wednesday.



According to police the parents of the child were nearby when the car was stolen.

It was later ditched with the child still inside after the suspect allegedly fled the area.



Police found the vehicle near Woodlesford Lock in Leeds within 15 minutes of the reported theft.

The young child was found in the car and looked after by responding officers.

The keys to the motor were left in the ignition by the suspect when they abandoned it.

West Yorkshire Police said no arrests have been made and enquiries into the horrifying incident remain ongoing.

The force added: “Officers received reports of a stolen car at around 8.30pm last night (5 August).

“The car was stolen from Long Thorpe Lane, Wakefield, and a child was in the car.



“Within approximately fifteen minutes of the report the police recovered the car near Woodlesford Lock, Leeds, and the child was returned to their family safely.

“Enquiries are currently ongoing.”

News.title: Benidorm breakfast buffet bandit is caught after ‘swiping Brits’ bags when they left tables to get their morning grub’
News.content:
CAUGHT BREAD HANDED Benidorm breakfast buffet bandit is caught after ‘swiping Brits’ bags when they left tables to get their morning grub’

A SHAMELESS alleged thief accused of pinching bags off Brits while they were serving themselves breakfast has been arrested.

The rampage of breakfast thefts spread across several different hotels in Benidorm.



The 43-year-old scoped out his victims from outside the breakfast bar, cops say.

More than a dozen bags and belongings were allegedly snatched off the backs of chairs and smuggled away under the suspect‘s clothes.



The suspected bandit hid his suspicious movements under a garment while allegedly robbing guests, reported local paper Diario Alicante.

Tourists reported the thief to the cops, who allegedly carried out crimes during breakfast buffet serving hours.

Cops connected the dots and realised that the thief was operating under “the same modus operandi”.

Police said: “All of them indicated that while they were having breakfast in the dining rooms of different hotels, they left their handbags hanging on the backs of their chairs and, when they got up for a few moments to serve themselves breakfast, they found upon returning that their belongings had disappeared.”

Brit families are among the alleged victims of the early-morning fiend.

The thief used the “distraction theft method” in order to steal “handbags, phones, or wallets of hotel guests”, cops say.



They added: “The alleged perpetrator previously selected his victims from the area outside the dining rooms.

“Once he spotted an opportunity, he entered the establishment and headed to the chosen table.

“After taking advantage of the moment when the victim was away, he positioned himself next to the back of the chair and, using a garment as a ‘cover’ to conceal his movements, stole the handbag without arousing suspicion, later leaving the place with the stolen items hidden under the aforementioned garment.



Following an investigation, cops arrested the sandal-wearing suspect.

He has been charged with 15 counts of theft.

Police have not ruled out the possibility that he may have committed more thefts as yet uncovered, reported local media.

The name and nationality of the suspect has not been made public.

He has already been brought to court in the town of Benidorm.



Cops in the US had a much harder time chasing down a suspected thief – who lead them in circles around a tree.

In what may have been the world’s slowest police chase, a siren-blaring cop car can be seen hunting down another vehicle – manned by a 14-year-old.

Footage shows the driver doing loop-de-loops around a tree while the police tail behind.

News.title: 'Ryanair left my life-saving luggage back in UK – I thought I'd die'
News.content:
'Ryanair left my life-saving luggage back in UK – I thought I'd die'

Ryanair had to fly out a passenger's critical piece of medical equipment after it was accidentally left behind in the UK

View 4 Images Samantha Mitchell's dialysis machine was left behind by Ryanair when she went on holiday (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

A woman was left in tears after discovering Ryanair left her dialysis machine in the UK after landing on holiday – fearing without it she would die.

‌



Samantha Mitchell, 39, flew from London Stansted to Reggio Calabria in southern Italy for a two-week holiday on July 26. However, upon her arrival in the country, she realised her 43kg dialysis machine was missing. Samantha, an SEN teacher, requires dialysis five times a week because she has kidney failure.

‌



This means, without the machine, she could have been in serious trouble. She even started phoning local hospitals to see if they had a machine as she was due to have dialysis at 5pm that evening.

‌



Samantha was in tears as Ryanair staff contacted Stansted airport, fearing she could have a heart attack without the treatment, and was later told it would be sent the following day.

The airline flew the machine out and sent it via taxi to her accommodation by the end of the following day, but by this point Samantha claims she was unwell and 'swelling up' from toxins.

Ryanair said the machine wasn't loaded due to "an error made by the check-in agent" but as soon as they were alerted "rushed" it onto the next available flight.

‌



She explained: “I've travelled with it [the machine] many times. I don't think they realised how serious it was that they had done this, it was full on panic and anxiety [mode]. I had to stop drinking and eating because I didn't want any more toxins in my body. I had started to swell up because I didn't pass urine and felt a bit sickly.”

View 4 Images Samantha's dialysis machine (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

Samantha, from Stoke-on-Trent, explained she risked a heart attack without the machine, she said: "Without it I would be very swollen and it would have become hard to breathe. I would start being sick and the worst thing would be a heart attack as the toxins in my blood would be too much.

‌



"I was literally fearing for my life. I was crying because I was panicking, my machine was all the way in London."

Recounting her check-in experience she said she was told her 43kg machine would be too heavy to go in the cabin, but that when she asked it to go in the hold, they said it would be okay.

She recalled: “I went to check-in my machine, [the agent] rang supervisors to make sure everything was okay and the documentation was okay. He said it was all fine and they'd take it through.

‌



"As soon as I got through security, they were asking for me to go back and speak to a supervisor about how heavy my machine was. It was 43kg, the supervisor said it was too heavy to go in the cabin with me but I wanted it in the hold. She said [that] was fine and it would go in the plane.”

View 4 Images Samantha needs dialysis five times a week (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

However, when she got to Italy, she received a phone call from her father who’d received an email saying the machine hadn’t gone in the plane because of its weight, at which point she and her family called Ryanair’s baggage team.

‌



Once Ryanair had been notified of the error they said they immediately sent the device onto the next flight out to the region and then delivered it by taxi to Samantha. They said the device had not been loaded due to an “error” by the check-in agent.

Following the experience Samantha said it had been “traumatic”, that she was worried for the flight back, and admitted it had put her off travelling.

She said: "It's been a very traumatic experience, a horrible start to the holiday. I am scared of the way back, it makes me not want to travel again in my life."

‌



View 4 Images Samantha (second from right) on holiday in Italy with mum Elaine, dad Malcolm and niece Roxanne

Samantha’s worry was echoed by her mother Elaine who said they rang the baggage team only to be told the device was too heavy. She recounted: “This is not a case of clothes gone missing, this is a life-saving machine. It was traumatic for all of us. We immediately rang the baggage team [...]and they told us it's a matter of health and safety.

“We were saying 'she's got a waiver, it's not a health and safety issue, it's a life and death issue.' If Sam doesn't have dialysis, she will be ill or worse. All [they] kept saying was that it was too heavy."

Article continues below

A Ryanair spokesman said: "Due to an error made by the check-in agent at Stansted Airport, this passenger’s medical device was not loaded on this flight from Stansted to Reggio Calabria (26 Jul).

"As soon this check-in agent’s error was realised, Ryanair rushed the device onto the next available flight to Reggio Calabria via Lamezia and arranged for a taxi to swiftly deliver the device directly to the passenger, which she received the following day (27 Jul)."

News.title: UK trains cancelled LIVE: Commuters braced for Friday delays after power outage
News.content:

Rail passengers are bracing for another day of travel chaos with a power outage bringing trains to a standstill across the Midlands and northwest of England.
