British number one Christian Medina Murphy has hailed the significant turnout at this week’s inaugural London P1 tournament as "amazing news" for the burgeoning sport of padel in the UK.

The event, marking England’s first professional padel competition, is expected to draw over 20,000 spectators to the Olympia venue in Kensington by its conclusion on Sunday.

Medina Murphy, a wild card entry, delighted home fans on Tuesday with a historic victory alongside his partner Alberto Garcia Jimenez on the opening day of the main draw.

Although the pair ultimately exited the tournament in the last 32 on Wednesday night, the experience was a memorable one for the world number 173.

open image in gallery Padel is becoming increasingly popular ( Getty )

The London P1, organised by the Saudi Arabian entertainment, events and sports marketing company Sela, represents the first Premier Padel event hosted in the UK.

Kingston upon Thames-born Medina Murphy was one of 11 British male and female players to participate, relishing the opportunity to compete on home soil. He expressed excitement not only for the future of London P1 but also for his own progress with Garcia Jimenez, following their recent FIP Bronze success at an Alicante event last month.

Reflecting on their 6-2 6-1 loss to 10th seeds Juan Tello and Maxi Arce, which concluded in 63 minutes on Court Two, Medina Murphy stated: "A lot of things to take. First of all I saw a lot of people here in the first days watching, supporting me and supporting all the players and I think that is amazing news for UK Padel."

He added: "I think in our level and looking to our level, I think we perform really good. We won the first round and that is really good performance. Yeah, really excited to be fighting against the best in the world and let’s see what is coming next. We perform well and have to train a little bit more to have more chances."

Padel is a sport that combines the skills used in tennis and squash. It originated in Mexico back in 1968 and has become increasingly popular across the globe in recent years, including in the UK.

News.title: 9 best supermarket wines right now, according to sommeliers and experts
News.content:
Good wine doesn’t have to be expensive. Supermarkets are full of great bottles now, whether you want a fresh white wine for drinking outside or a big glass of red wine to pair with a Sunday roast.

With feeds full of genuinely good, low-cost bottles, social media has played a big part in making wine feel more accessible. From the viral £10.99 “chicken wine” (La Vieille Ferme rosé) to Aldi’s award-winning sauvignon blanc and Asda’s playful alternative to Whispering Angel, Screaming Devil, plenty of bottles have blown up online and actually live up to the hype.

TikTok personalities like Lucy Hitchcock, known as @Partnerinwineuk, frequently cause bottles to dry out at M&S and Waitrose, as their recommendations fly off the shelves. Meanwhile, wine influencers like Hannah Crosbie and Tom Gilbey are helping strip away the snobbery, making wine feel far more accessible to everyday drinkers.

“Wine is a whole aisle now, as people want more variety as well as value, and supermarkets have wisely chosen to invest in their wine buyers and relationships with producers – because this is how most of us buy our wine,” says Libby Brodie, wine consultant and columnist. The same can be said with supermarket champagne and whisky, where growing demand has led to a wider selection and higher-quality offerings.

According to Sinead Murdoch, sommelier and co-founder of restaurant Tasca, supermarkets are increasingly appealing to more discerning drinkers. “Now top wine buyers are working for supermarkets, and the growing competition is raising the standard of what ends up on the shelves.” This means that shoppers can now find bottles that rival those in specialist wine shops, without having to spend a fortune or hunt for rare finds.

That said, it can still be hard to know what to pick up, so to make things easier, we spoke to the experts. Below, sommeliers and trusted wine voices share their top supermarket wine picks. Read on for what’s worth adding to your basket right now.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

Sports.title: Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero

Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero

Tottenham are open to selling Cristian Romero before the summer transfer window closes and Arsenal have emerged as surprise suitors amid their search for defensive reinforcements

Tottenham will refuse to sell Cristian Romero to Arsenal, who are interested in signing the Spurs captain. Romero, 28, is a shock target for the Gunners, who want to sign a centre-back before the transfer window shuts on September 1.

‌



Atletico Madrid and Inter Milan are also interested, with the latter striking a €40million (£34.2m) deal in principle with Tottenham. Romero, however, is yet to agree personal terms with Inter like he reportedly has with Atletico, who are preparing a bid of their own.

‌



According to The Athletic, Spurs were unaware of Arsenal's interest but would consider any transfer between the North London rivals a non-starter. William Gallas is the last player to move directly between the two clubs, joining Spurs in 2010 after his deal with Arsenal had expired.

‌



Sol Campbell controversially went the other way in 2001, having run down his contract at Tottenham. The transfer remains infamous to this day.

Rodri has spent seven years with City, winning four Premier League titles, one Champions League and two FA Cups. The former ex-Villarreal man received the Ballon d'Or in 2024, having won that year's European Championship with Spain.

Sports.title: Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has split world football this summer, with football associations sharing statements about his premiership, with Argentina and England again at odds

Gianni Infantino retains FIFA board’s support after crisis meeting

The Argentine Football Association have shared a statement in support of FIFA president Gianni Infantino's premiership over the last decade. That stance is at odds with the Football Association, who are withdrawing support for his re-election to a fourth term, much like the Football Association of Wales (FAW).

‌



The Football Associations of Finland, Serbia and Sweden have also done likewise ahead of the 77th FIFA Congress in mid-March. That is when the next presidential election will take place in Morocco.

‌



Denmark and Norway also oppose his re-election. Argentina, however, have now joined Egypt and several others in publicly supporting Infantino.

‌



View 2 Images Lionel Messi's Argentina have backed FIFA president Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

The AFA statement, translated into English from Spanish, reads: "Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the FIFA board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model. stable and transparent.

"In this sense, in relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the Administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties.

‌



"That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations of FIFA. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between FIFA, its member associations and the confederations.

View 2 Images The Confederation of African Football have backed Gianni Infantino, too (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

"In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of FIFA, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

‌



"From our point of view, this transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practice our beloved sport.

"Accordingly, with the upcoming FIFA Congress approaching, the Association that I proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The FA's last public statement was made last weekend regarding the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal being withdrawn by Infantino. They also acknowledged a statement from UEFA welcoming the move.

An FA spokesperson said: "We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has not yet followed transfer instructions previously laid out by Paul Scholes

View 4 Images Manchester United boss Michael Carrick was told by a former team-mate to sell some players (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick has not sanctioned any major sales so far this summer at Manchester United. This is despite United hero Paul Scholes recommending eight stars be sold.

Carrick is currently taking charge of his first pre-season and there are just a few weeks until the Premier League returns. With only three first-team signings made so far in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow, more additions are expected.

However, there has yet to be a major exit from the club, aside from Casemiro's departure. In April, Scholes was asked for a series of United stars who were surplus to requirements and of the eight players he listed, only one appears set to leave as things stand.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

7 Man Utd players face uncertain futures as part of huge summer overhaul of squad READ MORE :

Jadon Sancho's Man Utd decline and manager trend leaves unwanted star in awkward spot READ MORE :

Joshua Zirkzee was among the players that Scholes believed should be sold and the former Bologna forward is edging closer to a return to Italy. La Gazzetta dello Sport claims that Zirkzee is willing to join Juventus, who are pursuing a loan arrangement with an option to buy.

View 4 Images Zirkzee could be on the move soon (Image: Getty)

Scholes and Carrick spent seven seasons together in United's midfield during their playing days. However, whilst the pundit's suggestion to move on Zirkzee may materialise, the other seven stars Scholes mentioned could all remain part of United's squad next term, with Carrick's response clear.

The 51-year-old stressed the importance of United revamping their defence. Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast, Scholes said of Leny Yoro: "I think he's struggled, me. I think there's something in there, I think he needs a bit of time, but if you had to make a choice now, I'd probably sell him."

He also argued that the shift away from ex-boss Ruben Amorim's three-at-the-back system would have implications for Noussair Mazraoui. Mazraoui has been linked with a departure this summer, though he remains part of Carrick's side. Highly-rated defender Yoro has also expressed a desire to make his mark at United next season.

View 4 Images Yoro was a surprise inclusion (Image: Getty)

Turning to midfield, Scholes felt Manuel Ugarte would depart and the Uruguayan was linked with a move before picking up an injury at the World Cup. Mason Mount also featured on Scholes' eight-man list, though the England international has caught the eye during pre-season.

Additionally, Scholes felt the moment had arrived to say goodbye to Harry Maguire, who continues to have a key role at United. He said: "I'm thinking about a Manchester United team you want to win the league and the Champions League and that's where United should be aiming. I'm not sure you'd do that with Maguire."

Elsewhere, United have held an interest in Newcastle United full-back Lewis Hall in the transfer window. Focusing on the left-back position, Scholes previously urged the club to offload long-serving Luke Shaw due to doubts about his reliability, despite him having featured in every Premier League fixture last season. He was equally prepared to let Patrick Dorgu leave.

View 4 Images Mount, Shaw and Maguire were three of the players that Scholes named (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Scholes said on Dorgu: "They brought him in as a wing-back and he's not really played much there. I'd probably sell. I'm not sure what position he is. Again, if you keep him then he's just a squad player."

Overall, of the eight players Scholes recommended be sold, only Zirkzee appears set for an imminent exit. There has been little speculation regarding the remaining seven of Yoro, Mazraoui, Shaw, Dorgu, Mount, Ugarte and Maguire.

Sports.title: Arsenal's 10 highest Premier League sales – and why it speaks volumes for Andrea Berta
Sports.content:
Arsenal's 10 highest Premier League sales – and why it speaks volumes for Andrea Berta

Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has plenty on his plate as the Premier League champions bid to kick on this summer

View 4 Images Andrea Berta has a lot on his plate as Arsenal's sporting director (Image: Getty)

Arsenal's sporting director Andrea Berta has overseen some important signings since joining the club, with more expected to follow. But sales have been a challenge for the Gunners, with the problem persisting long before the Italian took up the role.

‌



The north London side's record sale still sits at just £35million. To put that into context, only three of the other 19 Premier League sides - Sunderland, Hull and Coventry - have lower records. Arsenal simply aren't selling well.

‌



A total of three sales this summer have raised less than £40m combined, with Karl Hein, Jakub Kiwior and Leandro Trossard completing permanent exits. Arsenal have already paid in the region of £34m for both Piero Hincapie and Christos Tzolis, whilst the anticipated move for Bruno Guimaraes will see them more than double their outlay.

‌



When it comes to record sales, it's telling that the top four spots are occupied by transfers from the Arsene Wenger era, and the club simply aren't keeping up with the big-money exits that clubs like Chelsea and Manchester City sanction. Here are their 10 most lucrative offloadings, in reverse order, per Transfermarkt figures.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Two Champions League rule changes announced by UEFA ahead of new season READ MORE :

Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club READ MORE :

10. Joe Willock (£25.2m)

Willock's move to Newcastle was a case of striking whilst the iron was hot. The midfielder scored eight goals during a loan spell at St James' Park, driving up his value and convincing Arsenal to cash in.

‌



The England Under-21 international hasn't yet matched that goal tally across more than 100 games as a permanent Newcastle player, though his role became far less attacking under Eddie Howe. He was used sparingly last term, struggling to displace Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali.

9. Eddie Nketiah (£25.4m)

Another recent sale, Nketiah demonstrated Premier League pedigree in an Arsenal shirt when he scored a hat-trick against Sheffield United in 2023. Months later, Crystal Palace took the plunge with a big-money bid and the striker - battling with the likes of Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus for opportunities - decided to try his luck elsewhere.

View 4 Images Nketiah is about to embark on his third season at Crystal Palace (Image: Getty)

‌



Get Arsenal's new 2026/27 home kit This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £85 Fanatics Buy Now on Fanatics Product Description Arsenal have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27 season, said to incorporate classic Arsenal design features that tie into the club's heritage.

The Eagles could end up paying even more for the England international if conditions for add-ons are met. However, his second season at Selhurst Park was cut short by injury and he will hope for a fresh start under new boss Pierre Sage.

8. Folarin Balogun (£25.7m)

Balogun, like Nketiah, moved in search of more regular first-team football. Again, Arsenal got good money for a fringe player when he followed up a 21-goal Ligue 1 season at Reims with a move to their rivals Monaco.

‌



The United States international top-scored for his club last term and thrived for his country at the World Cup. There's no guarantee he would have developed at the same speed in North London, though.

7. Alex Iwobi (£26m)

Academy graduate Iwobi grew into his role at Arsenal, scoring in the 2019 Europa League final defeat to Chelsea and playing 100 league games for the Gunners. But the arrival of Nicolas Pepe meant he was considered disposable.

Marco Silva signed the Nigerian international for Everton but was gone within months in a tough first season. Things have gone better for Iwobi after a reunion with Silva at Fulham, where he has thrived in a deeper midfield role than the one he occupied at his boyhood club.

‌



6. Robin van Persie (£26.3m)

View 4 Images Van Persie's United move was one of 2012's most talked-about transfers (Image: Getty)

The £26m paid by Manchester United for Van Persie in 2012 was worth a great deal more then than now. Still, it's telling that a deal from more than a decade ago is one of the top 10 on this list. And it's not the only one.

The Dutch striker's move was hugely dramatic at the time, with plenty of fans turning on a former favourite. United will have considered the move a success after his goals brought an immediate league title but the following two years were less fruitful for player and club and he left for Fenerbahce in 2015.

‌



5. Emile Smith Rowe (£27.2m)

Academy graduate Smith Rowe made a fast start as a teenager but found himself overtaken in the pecking order during Mikel Arteta's tenure. He left for Fulham in 2024, with Mikel Merino brought in by Arteta just weeks later.

The three-cap England international has remained a solid presence in Fulham's midfield, featuring in 71 of 76 available league matches. However, he has not looked close to a Three Lions recall, nearly four years on from his most recent cap.

‌



4. Cesc Fabregas (£29.1m)

Your eyes don't deceive you. That's a 2011 sale in the top five - by way of comparison, Chelsea have sold 20 players for more money since then, give or take the margin of error for conversions between Euros and Pounds.

It was one of two big-money moves for Fabregas in his career, with the Spaniard also joining Chelsea in 2014 for a similar amount to the Barcelona deal after Arsenal opted against bringing him back. He won two Premier League titles with the Blues and has now made an impressive start to his managerial career with Como.

3. Alexis Sanchez (£29.1m)

You might not even want to count this one, given the fact that it came as part of an effective swap deal. We're leaving it in just to emphasise the task facing Berta as he looks to succeed where his predecessors struggled.

‌



Sanchez moved to United in 2018, with Henrikh Mkhitaryan joining Arsenal from the Red Devils. The Londoners came out of the deal a little better but neither club had huge success from the arrangement.

2. Nicolas Anelka (£30m)

Those tricky conversion fees mean reports vary for how much Anelka went for in Pounds. Even so, it says a lot that a sale from 1999 features on this list.

View 4 Images Anelka joined Real Madrid more than a quarter of a century ago (Image: Getty)

‌



Anelka was an example of Arsenal turning a huge profit on a player they signed for less than £1m from Paris Saint-Germain. He would go on to make more than 500 career league appearances across several countries and also played for France at the World Cup and European Championships.

1. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain (£35m)

Arsenal's record sale remains the £35m they received when Oxlade-Chamberlain joined Liverpool in 2017. The England international became a Premier League and Champions League winner during his time at Anfield but was plagued by injury.

Despite spending six years as a Liverpool player, he made just 103 league appearances. He left for Besiktas on a free transfer in 2023 and is now at Celtic.

Sports.title: Liverpool were linked with World Cup winner and £53m star for ages but never signed them
Sports.content:
Liverpool were linked with World Cup winner and £53m star for ages but never signed them

Transfer sagas spanning years is a situation Liverpool know a thing or two about

View 5 Images Nabil Fekir's failed move to Liverpool was shrouded in controversy (Image: NurPhoto/PA Images)

Few things ignite the football world quite like a transfer saga, and Liverpool have certainly starred in their fair share over the years. There's been plenty of wins in the market for the Reds, such as their past acquisitions of Mohamed Salah and Sadio Mane, or besting Bayern Munich to the signing of Florian Wirtz last summer.

‌



High-stakes moves trigger an intense mix of fan hype and deadline-day anxiety, but the tension usually dissolves the second a player hits the pitch in red. Every so often, however, years of following a particular target and intense negotiations end in heartbreak.

‌



From controversial collapses of deals to players simply opting for another club, Mirror Football takes a look at five targets Liverpool failed to drag across the finish line - and why the deals fell apart.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Nabil Fekir

Arguably the most infamous collapsed transfer in recent Liverpool history, the breakdown of Nabil Fekir's switch to Anfield in 2018 sparked accusations of dishonesty and family drama. The Frenchman had undergone a medical ahead of his £53million transfer from Lyon and agreed personal terms before the Reds pulled out of the deal.

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

Man Utd forced to fork out millions as Marcus Rashford benefits from contract loophole READ MORE :

The attacking midfielder had even posed for promotional photographs with the club, who insisted their decision to abandon the deal was down to a knee cartilage issue. Fekir dismissed the Reds' explanation as a lie and rejected claims from his then-agent, Jean-Pierre Bernes, who suggested that the Frenchman's brother-in-law tried to secure a cut from the transfer.

‌



"Lots of lies were told, and they affected me," Fekir told L'Equipe in 2019. "Especially those told about my family. It hurt them and me. Especially when you know that what's being told is false.

"What was said is not the truth. My knee is good - I had a quick medical check at Clairefontaine [the headquarters of France's national team] - my knee wasn't even mentioned. If my knee had been in such a bad state, would [then-Lyon chairman Jean-Michel Aulas] have made [a sufficient offer to keep the player]?"

Gareth Barry

View 5 Images Gareth Barry was wanted twice by Rafael Benitez (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Countdown to Kickoff: The Ultimate 26/27 Sky Sports Bundle This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £44 Sky Get the deal here Product Description Sky's Ultimate TV and Sky Sports bundle includes at least 215 live Premier League clashes across the 2026/27 season with more than 1,400 live games across the EFL and beyond, plus F1, golf and darts. Every subscription now comes with 135 channels alongside free subscriptions to HBO Max, Netflix, Disney+, discovery+ and Hayu.

Liverpool's pursuit of Gareth Barry began in the summer of 2008. A vital component of Aston Villa's midfield engine room, Rafael Benitez had identified the Englishman as the ideal replacement for Xabi Alonso, who had endured an injury-disrupted campaign throughout 2007/08.

Yet the Reds fell short of Villa's £18m valuation for their skipper, forcing Barry to remain at the Midlands club. Liverpool returned to the negotiating table twelve months on, with their persistent interest in the midfielder ultimately prompting Alonso to seal a switch to Real Madrid.

‌



It proved a double setback for Benitez as Barry chose Manchester City over Anfield. Reflecting on his decision to snub Liverpool, Barry told Birmingham Live's Claret and Blue podcast: "Something appealed to me more about Man City than Liverpool at the time. Liverpool had won the Champions League not so long ago and Man City hadn't won a trophy for many years, but I went with that route."

Arda Turan

View 5 Images Arda Turan was linked to the Reds during his time at Galatasaray and Atletico Madrid (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

Arda Turan was repeatedly linked with a switch to Liverpool over a six-year period between 2009 and 2015. The speculation started during his stint at Galatasaray, but it was Atletico Madrid who secured his services in 2011.

‌



His impressive four-year spell in the Spanish capital, which featured their La Liga triumph in 2014, didn't halt talk of his possible arrival on Merseyside, according to AS. It was claimed the Turkish star grew up watching Liverpool and his father supported the club.

Despite his family's reported affection for the Reds, Turan never turned out for the club and instead moved to Barcelona in 2015, before hanging up his boots in 2022 with Galatasaray.

Simao Sabrosa

We're turning back the clock with Simao Sabrosa. A prominent figure in Portuguese football during the 2000s, the former forward came within touching distance of joining the Reds in the summer of 2005 before Benfica pulled out of the arrangement.

‌



A reported £10m deal had been struck between the two clubs, with Simao even leaving Portugal's training camp to undergo a medical. The 46-year-old opened up about the collapsed transfer in 2022, when speaking to Liverpoolfc.com.

He recounted: "At that time I'm in the national team, three or four days until the end [of the window]. I received a call at like five o'clock in the morning, 'You need to come, we go to Liverpool.'

View 5 Images Simao Sabrosa was inches away from becoming a Liverpool player (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

‌



"I go to [Luiz Felipe] Scolari and the director of the national team to give me permission to go out. When I go to the office of my agent, in that moment the president of Benfica called and said, 'We don't have a deal, you don't have permission to fly, so you need to stay.'

"It's strange because I thought it was done. But when the president went home, he called again and said, 'It's impossible to fly to Liverpool and get a new contract with Liverpool, so you need to stay. Because if you sign for Liverpool, Benfica fans will be angry [with me].' At that time I said, 'OK, I stay.'

"The office of my agent is near the airport and the agent gave me some impression, 'Let's go to the airport. When we arrive in Liverpool, maybe the president says yes.' I said, 'No, it's impossible to take the plane and fly to Liverpool.'

‌



"I was representing the national team and if I take this decision, I have a lot of problems with the national team, my club, so I decided to stay." His switch to Atletico Madrid in 2007 did little to silence ongoing speculation of a transfer to Anfield, but nothing advanced as close as it had a year prior.

Julian Draxler

The former Germany international is another footballer familiar to Liverpool supporters. The 32-year-old, who presently features for Qatari outfit Al-Ahli, emerged into the spotlight with boyhood side Schalke in 2011, which is when his enduring connections to Liverpool commenced.

Former Reds manager Brendan Rodgers reportedly made a personal trip to the Veltins-Arena to run the rule over Draxler during a Champions League clash against Basel. However, a deal never came to fruition as the attacking midfielder ultimately joined fellow Bundesliga outfit Wolfsburg in 2015.

‌



View 5 Images Julian Draxler opted to join Paris Saint-Germain (Image: Getty Images)

A switch to Paris Saint-Germain followed two years on, though not before Liverpool had once again registered their interest in the 2014 World Cup winner, this time under Jurgen Klopp. The German tactician was eager to bring compatriot Draxler to Merseyside, but the player chose a move to the French capital instead.

He has since admitted to pondering what might have unfolded had he chosen to test himself in the Premier League. "When I was still very young at Schalke and extended my contract, I could have gone to Arsenal," he told BILD, as quoted by Sport Witness.

Article continues below

"Honestly, I'd be interested to see what would have become of me if I had learned from Arsene Wenger so early. I've also wondered what would have happened if I hadn't gone from Wolfsburg to Paris, but to Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool. I had that opportunity, too. Nevertheless, I'm happy. I'm at peace with my decisions."

Sports.title: Man Utd dream attack as Marcus Rashford exits plus free agent striker and World Cup star join
Sports.content:
Man Utd dream attack as Marcus Rashford exits plus free agent striker and World Cup star join

Manchester United continue their hard work in the summer transfer window with more players on the way

View 4 Images Marcus Rashford's Manchester United future is still up in the air (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Manchester United could offload Marcus Rashford's hefty wages and a struggling striker to make way for more new signings to arrive at Old Trafford. The Red Devils are continuing their activity in the summer transfer window with Michael Carrick building a squad capable of competing across various competitions.

‌



United have spent £83m so far this summer, and have seen some huge salaries drop off the wage bill. Jadon Sancho departed the club as a free agent and Casemiro headed for Inter Miami, both of which freed up some room in the budget.

‌



A £35m move for Youri Tielemans has been completed, with the former Aston Villa midfielder signing a five-year deal at Old Trafford. Andrey Santos also joined from Chelsea for an initial £48m, plus £2m in add-ons to beef up the middle of the park.

‌



Karl Darlow, Kit Margetson and Tynan Thompson have also arrived. However, Carrick will still be eager for more players through the door. Some stars will have to depart to accommodate this, with Rashford's future one of a number up for discussion.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Man Utd closing in on transfer deal after Michael Carrick dropped hint READ MORE :

Joshua Zirkzee is also being linked with a switch to Juventus, though only on a temporary basis. Reinforcements will be required for Carrick to have enough squad depth to compete both at home and in Europe.

Here, Mirror Football has looked at what a dream United attacking lineup could look like this season.

Free agent striker

United signed Zirkzee for £36.5m in 2024 but he has slipped down the pecking order at Old Trafford. The Dutchman has made a few appearances under Carrick but watched on as Benjamin Sesko leapfrogged him to spearhead the attack last season.

‌



Italian newspaper Corriere dello Sport reports that Juventus are closing in on a loan deal for Zirkzee, with boss Luciano Spalletti 'saying yes' to the move. It looks increasingly likely that the former Bologna man will depart this summer, one way or another.

United will likely need reinforcements if that is to happen, although Carrick may not want to disrupt the progress of Sesjo, who impressed towards the back end of last term. This is where the free agency market could prove invaluable. Dusan Vlahovic is one among several forwards who have been linked to Old Trafford – and he could represent the perfect signing for nothing at all.

View 4 Images Dusan Vlahovic represents a cheap but effective option (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



The 26-year-old left Juve following the expiry of his deal this summer, having netted 68 goals in 168 outings. He has amassed 140 club goals throughout his career.

Vlahovic boasts a considerable European pedigree but could provide adequate cover for Sesko, who has impressed under Carrick's guidance. Securing a free agent would demonstrate the manager's faith in the Slovenian forward while allowing him to develop through competition with the Serbia international.

Vlahovic would additionally offer greater flexibility in attack, enabling Carrick to rest Sesko and maintain squad fitness throughout a demanding campaign.

‌

Sky broadcasts more than 1,400 live matches across the Premier League, EFL and more with at least 215 live from the top flight alongside Formula 1, darts and golf.

Rashford decision

Rashford's situation at United continues to hang in the balance. At present, the academy product is set to rejoin pre-season preparations with the club following the collapse of a Barcelona switch.

He remains heavily linked with a move away from the club, including in recent days to Fenerbahce. Earlier in the window, however, it was thought that Rashford wouldn't be keen on a move to Turkey, which could put the skids on any potential move before it has even gotten going. Tottenham have also registered their interest, and with several weeks remaining before the transfer window shuts, whether Rashford's future lies at Old Trafford or beyond remains very much unresolved.

‌



View 4 Images Iliman Ndiaye's experience would be greatly welcomed at Old Trafford (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images)

Should he depart permanently, Iliman Ndiaye could prove an ideal replacement, bringing with him solid Premier League pedigree. The 26-year-old has racked up 20 goal contributions across 70 appearances for Everton and is strongly linked with a move to United.

It is understood that the Toffees will hold out for around £70m for the left-winger, who is also attracting attention from Saudi Pro League outfit Al-Hilal.

‌



United's dream attack

View 4 Images United's attacking is shaping up quite nicely (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

With Benjamin Sesko currently leading the line, Vlahovic could be the ideal option for United to call upon when needed. With two top-quality strikers at their disposal, focus would then shift to the wide positions.

Amad and Bryan Mbeumo have the right flank well covered, with the latter likely to get the nod to start. Ndiaye would fit seamlessly on the left, and there is always the option to utilise Patrick Dorgu in a more advanced role after impressing last season.

Article continues below

Regarding the No. 10 role in Carrick's favoured 4-2-3-1 system, Bruno Fernandes will continue as the dependable playmaker and club captain.

Sports.title: Gibbs' Lions deal makes him NFL's highest-paid running back ever
Sports.content:
Jahmyr Gibbs is set to become the highest-paid running back in NFL history having agreed to a new three-year deal worth up to $75.7m (£56.3m) with the Detroit Lions.

Gibbs' agents Athletes First announced the deal Thursday, hours after he took the field for the first time since the Lions' training camp started. His agents also noted the new contract includes $51.5m (£38.3m) guaranteed for the Pro Bowler.

Two days earlier, Atlanta briefly made Bijan Robinson the NFL's highest-paid running back in history.

Gibbs had been participating in meetings at camp, but Thursday was his first appearance on the field, an indication the Lions and his agents were close to a deal. Gibbs held his right arm high and gave a thumbs-up when asked if an agreement was close as he walked off the practice field.

Gibbs changed his jersey number from 26 to 0 ahead of the 2025 season and rushed for 1,223 yards and 13 touchdowns, and had 77 receptions for 616 yards and five scores.

Sports.title: Undrafted King leads Panthers to comeback win vs Cardinals in Hall of Fame game
Sports.content:
Undrafted rookie quarterback Haynes King ran in on the final play to give the Carolina Panthers a 33-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals in the Hall of Fame game that kicked off the NFL preseason on Thursday night.

King, who was the Atlantic Coast Conference Player of the Year last season at Georgia Tech, was 21 of 34 for 180 yards and two touchdowns. He ran for 39 yards and the winning score.

"Well, that was a lot of fun. Just the back and forth of it. Just a really good game," Panthers coach Dave Canales said.

"The guys were resilient and finish is what we preach as a team. We practice for these situations, end of half, end of game. Haynes did a fantastic job, just keeping the play alive, doing whatever he had to do, run it, throw it. Really proud of the group."

Sports.title: Is red-hot Norrie now favourite to win Montreal? Brit dumps out third seed De Minaur

Five years on from winning his biggest title in Indian Wells, Britain's Cameron Norrie has found his form to dump out third seed Alex de Minaur and reach the fourth round of the National Bank Open in Montreal.

Down 7-5 5-2 with De Minaur on match point, Norrie turned the tables by winning 11 out of the next 13 games to beat the Australian 5-7 7-6 (7-5) 6-1.

Norrie, who has climbed above Arthur Fery to No 36 in the live rankings will become the new British No 1, but the former Wimbledon semi-finalist has ambitions of collecting the second Masters title of his career with Frenchman Arthur Fils up next.

Sports.title: Hearts humbled by Benfica as Hibs secure vital win; Motherwell held in Helsinki
Sports.content:
Hearts endured a predictably bruising evening in Lisbon as their hopes of progressing to the Europa League were all but ended by a 6-1 thrashing at the hands of Benfica.

After a largely demoralising summer, which began with being pipped to the William Hill Premiership title by Celtic in May, 1,300 embattled Jambos travelled to the Portuguese capital for one of the most formidable fixtures in the club's recent history, braced for a fourth consecutive defeat under new head coach Wouter Vrancken.

And that was exactly what transpired as Marco Silva's Benfica opened the scoring in the third minute, led by three at the break and then added another three in the second half to remove all sense of jeopardy from next Thursday's second leg at Tynecastle.

While the Portuguese giants are on course to face the losers of the Champions League tie between Aarhus and Sabah Baku in the Europa League play-off round, Hearts are staring at a likely Conference League play-off against Rapid Vienna, who lead Paide 4-1 after the first leg in Estonia.

Hibernian will take a valuable lead to North Macedonia for the second leg of their Conference League third qualifying round clash after overcoming Shkendija 2-1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hibernian head coach David Gray says his side will get even better as they beat Shkendija in the first leg of their Conference League third-round qualifier.

Hibs had gone in front in the 73rd minute through Owen Elding, only for the visitors to level less than three minutes later courtesy of Marko Gjorgjievski.

However, Warren O'Hora notched a 90th-minute winner when he bundled in a Jordan Obita corner to leave Hibs in a good position to reach the competition's play-off round when they make the trip to Skopje for the second leg.

Image: Warren O'Hora (L) celebrates after scoring to make it 2-1 to Hibs at Easter Road

Motherwell's impressive start under Alfred Johansson continued as they secured a 1-1 draw away to HJK Helsinki in the first leg of their Conference League third qualifying round tie.

The Lanarkshire side's new Swedish boss briefly looked on course for his fourth consecutive victory at the helm after Tawanda Maswanhise's penalty gave the Steelmen the lead just after the hour mark.

Image: Tawanda Maswanhise put Motherwell ahead in Helsinki

However, 36-year-old former Celtic and Norwich City striker Teemu Pukki equalised for Finnish side HJK within seconds of coming off the bench.

Motherwell, who lost Alex Lowry and Regan Charles-Cook to injuries in the closing stages, will return home believing they have a good chance of setting up a glamour play-off showdown with Europa League runners-up Freiburg later this month.

Sports.title: Barron scores hat-trick as Hull FC end losing run with win over St Helens
Sports.content:
Super League: Harvey Barron scores treble as Hull FC end losing run with win over St Helens

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of St Helens against Hull FC in the Betfred Super League Highlights of St Helens against Hull FC in the Betfred Super League

Winger Harvey Barron scored a first senior hat-trick as Hull FC ended a seven-game losing run with a 32-18 comeback win at St Helens.

Barron's treble boosted the Black and Whites' hopes of avoiding the Super League wooden spoon while casting further doubt on Saints making the end of season play-offs.

Hull had not previously won at the BrewDog Stadium in 10 games and nine years and sat just two points off bottom club Huddersfield Giants.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Player of the match Aidan Sezer conceded it's been a tough season after Hull FC ended their seven-match losing streak against St Helens Player of the match Aidan Sezer conceded it's been a tough season after Hull FC ended their seven-match losing streak against St Helens

However, in this battle of the interim coaches, Andy Last got the better of counterpart Eamon O'Carroll, who last weekend oversaw Saints' first defeat at York in more than 80 years.

Hull trailed 14-10 approaching half-time but Barron struck almost on the hooter and completed his career landmark hat-trick after 47 minutes before substitute Cade Cust crashed over three minutes later.

Those 16 points in 11 minutes stunned Saints, still reeling from last month's exit of Paul Rowley after less than a year as head coach.

Despite a first away victory on Saints' territory since August 2017, Hull stay 13th although they are now level on points with Bradford Bulls.

St Helens have never failed to reach the play-offs but they remain seventh with all teams above them to play in the coming days.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull FC interim head coach Andy Last said it felt fantastic for his side to end their losing streak Hull FC interim head coach Andy Last said it felt fantastic for his side to end their losing streak

They led three times in the opening 40 minutes but conceded their advantage each time and were fortunate to be level at 14-14.

The game's first mistake after barely two minutes saw full-back Logan Moy's knock-on punished by winger Lewis Murphy, who finished in the corner.

FC were behind only five minutes as Zak Hardaker's pass sent in Barron for the first of his treble.

Hastings edged Saints in front again with an 18th-minute penalty for Tom Briscoe's high tackle.

Prop Herman Ese'ese had a second Hull try ruled out for a double movement while he and Barron were repelled in quick succession before the visitors' deservedly hit the front.

Stand-off Jake Arthur's double cut-out pass freed Lewis Martin to finish in the left corner to make it 10-8.

Barron was denied again by last-gasp cover tackling and it was against the run of play when Jack Welsby raced 30 metres to touch down.

With 37 seconds remaining Saints captain Hastings dropped out. Thirty four seconds later Barron seized on Aidan Sezer's angled kick to cross again, waiting anxiously before video referee Chris Kendall overturned Liam Rush's on-field decision of 'no try'.

Tries for Barron and Cust, both converted by Hardaker, virtually put the contest out of reach.

By the time Harry Robertson scored a consolation try, Hardaker's 70th-minute penalty sealed the deal for Hull FC, who finished off with a further try from ex-Saint James Bell.

Jenna Foubister of Wigan celebrates their victory over St Helens

In the Women's Super League, Wigan Warriors saw off rivals St Helens 44-6 in the first match of the new Super Four format.

The defending champions outclassed St Helens with Ellise Derbyshire and Eva Hunter scoring a brace with further scores from Anna Davies, Molly Jones, Remi Wilton, Jenna Foubister and Mary Coleman at the BrewDog Stadium.

Sports.title: Britain's best prospect? Hickey is a real showman
Sports.content:
Sam Hickey is a real showman. In fact, he’s a member of the guild.

Hickey is one of the best boxing prospects in Britain. He was an outstanding amateur who won the Commonwealth Games, only to see to his weight class removed from the Olympics themselves.

Now a professional boxer, he is five fights into his career. He's displayed his sharp movement, strong counter-punching and spectacular finishing, especially in his last fight where he delivered a tremendous knockout of Todd Tompkins.

The Scotsman is from a family of showmen, the community that travels around the country operating fairgrounds and carnivals.

"Still got loads of family involved. I'm a member of the Showman's Guild, the Scottish section back home. I get a lot of support off the showmen all over the country, not just Scottish showmen and all my family. It's a big backing throughout the country," Hickey told Sky Sports.

"We do a lot of tickets all over the country and I've got so much backing from Dundee, everywhere in Scotland.

"There's loads of us. It's great to be doing that and putting them on the map and getting so much support as well."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hickey dropped Lewis Howells twice to the body before stopping his opponent in the opening round of their bout

That's what Hickey could be doing for a living now, rather than boxing, if his father hadn't settled in Dundee.

"My mum and dad packed it in just as I was born so I was growing up around the fairs. My cousins and that were all travelling in funfairs and I was still going and staying with them in the summers and that," Hickey reflected.

"I'm based in Dundee and I've been able to take up boxing and give it a proper go, but if my dad and mum were still travelling and working on fairs and had their own rides and stuff, maybe I'd be working on that."

He wants to follow in the footsteps of the great Scottish boxers who have preceded him. Hickey wants to fill the void left by the retirement of Josh Taylor. He wants to be Scotland's next boxing superstar.

"In Scottish boxing there's a few of us coming though," Hickey said. "I'd love to do what Josh, Ricky [Burns], all these great fighters from Scotland [have done]. They were all amazing fighters.

"I feel like I'm getting a lot more comfortable in the pro ring, getting my own style and developing as a fighter. Being more relaxed. I just feel like it's coming together now."

He comes from the same town as Dick McTaggart, the greatest British amateur boxer of all time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of his fight against Brad Axe, Hickey said he wants to become the new face of Scottish boxing

When Hickey was growing up as a youngster boxing on club shows, McTaggart would frequently come to watch and give him some advice. "He would just tell you to keep your hands up," Hickey remembered.

"[He had the] most achievements as an amateur over a long period of time, winning so many trophies and medals, the best boxer at an Olympic Games, then he goes to the next Olympics after that and wins a bronze, he still stayed on it. Back then there was no serious funding for amateur athletes, he was still working and stuff while doing all this.

"He always had his medal in his pocket and he would just hand it out like it was nothing, he just let you hold it.

"He never ever turned professional. I think it was because he loved the sport so much."

Hickey is only at the early stages of his own journey through boxing. On Saturday, live on Sky Sports, he fights Brad Axe on the undercard of Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha at the 3Arena in Dublin.

Axe is an ambitious prospect himself, with one defeat against six victories. An RAF firefighter, he won the Armed Forces championship as an amateur and is looking to derail Hickey's hopes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Johnny Nelson was full of praise for Hickey after his first-round victory over Howells, comparing him to boxing great Joe Calzaghe

"He's going to be tough, strong. But I've been exposed to really high-level boxing so I don't think it's going to be something that I've never seen before," Hickey said.

"Brad Axe is no mug, he's going to come to fight. But it's up to me… I really should be breaking him down."

Hickey would love to replicate the kind of knockout he landed against Tompkins. "I don't even realise what I'm doing. I watch it back and think: 'How did I do that?' Honestly I don't understand it, it's weird. Next thing they're on the floor," he said.

"It's timing, if they miss with a punch and you're connecting.

"Pro boxing's entertainment and you need to be putting on good performances," he added.

Axe should make for the kind of fight that can propel Hickey to a new level. "I need to be switched on from the start. It's going to stand me in good stead later on in my career as well," he said.

"I want to be in big shows in Scotland. If that comes sooner rather than later then that's the best thing for me.

"I just need to keep going, keep winning, enjoy the journey."

Sports.title: Uefa maintains World Cup boycott still stands despite Fifa’s backing for Infantino
Sports.content:
Uefa has doubled down on its threat to boycott Fifa-run competitions and reiterated its loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency.

The latest damning intervention from European football’s governing body came as criticism of Infantino continued to rain in from several angles. The global players’ union, Fifpro, condemned “a profound abuse of presidential power” while the South American confederation, Conmebol, usually a strong Infantino ally, was moved to chastise “repeated unilateral actions taken without resorting to dialogue”.

It is Uefa’s continued stance, though, that may damage Infantino most severely. In a statement it said Fifa’s public backing of Infantino on Wednesday night “changes nothing” and explained it was not convinced repeats of the past nine days’ crisis will not occur.

Last week Uefa’s 55 member associations agreed to boycott Fifa tournaments if Infantino did not withdraw his privately funded Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme and, although the plan was scrapped last Friday, it said the terms necessary to avert the boycott have not been met.

“Uefa’s associations were very clear about the conditions attached to their non-participation in Fifa competitions,” it said. “First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn and, secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

“These conditions have not been met. In addition, Uefa made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency. That position holds. Yesterday’s announcement that some people employed by the Fifa president (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing.”

It heightens the turmoil enveloping football’s governance. If no accord is reached before the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, which begins in Poland on 5 September, that would be the first tournament subjected to a Uefa-led boycott.

Uefa remains hopeful it can exploit divisions within Fifa’s leadership despite the Infantino-led show of unity following Wednesday’s meeting of some of its management board in Rabat.

There were several notable absentees, however, and it is understood that Arsène Wenger declined an invitation to travel to Morocco in his capacity as Fifa’s chief of global development because of a desire to distance himself from Infantino. The former Arsenal manager had launched a scathing attack on the World Cup sell-off plans, saying it was “absolutely necessary and beyond question” that they were scrapped.

In contrast to Wenger, Fifa’s chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, who had described the proposals as “the project of one person”, was not invited to the summit in a development that will raise further questions over his future. Additionally Jill Ellis, the chief football officer, and Sarai Bareman, the chief women’s football officer, were not present in Rabat.

While Fifa has sent apologies to the Fifa council and member associations for their exclusion from the FFE process, it is believed that those sentiments failed to sway a large percentage of council members.

A handful of Uefa federations have withdrawn letters of support for Infantino’s re-election for a fourth term, although the early rush to make such declarations has slowed. The Football Association has now written to Fifa formally retracting its backing.

Uefa’s repeat of its boycott threat was followed by a scathing release from Fifpro. Before the World Cup Fifpro signalled its intention to work with Fifa by signing a memorandum of understanding but that has proved the briefest of truces.

Alongside the criticism, Fifpro wrote to Fifa making a series of demands, including giving players voting rights on the Fifa council, which is supposed to be the main decision-making body but has often been bypassed by Infantino.

“Fifa Forward Enterprise is gone, but the abuse of power that produced it is not,” Fifpro said. “Governance reforms, not a cover-up, are urgently needed. The withdrawal of FFE was inevitable. But withdrawing the proposal does not erase what it revealed.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“A plan capable of permanently altering the ownership and governance of the Fifa World Cup … was conceived in secrecy, negotiated behind closed doors and brought to the brink of agreement before the Fifa council, the member associations, players and football’s recognised stakeholders even knew it existed. That is not merely a governance failure. It is a profound abuse of presidential power.”

Conmebol, three of whose members are in line to host matches at the 2030 World Cup, had waited more than a week to comment publicly. While its disapproval was clear it stopped short of pushing for immediate change.

In a statement it said the Conmebol council “unanimously expresses its concern regarding the repeated unilateral actions taken without resorting to dialogue or to the institutional mechanisms established to address situations of this nature”.

While Uefa is leading efforts to unseat Infantino before Fifa’s election in March, Conmebol pointed out the timeline for the process has already been set. “Accordingly, Conmebol will not support any action or procedure that disregards or departs from those institutional mechanisms,” it said.

Earlier on Thursday the Jordan Football Association president, Prince Ali bin al-Hussein, said Fifa had paid bonuses owed from last December’s Arab Cup but clarified he would still oppose Infantino.

The money appears to have materialised after Prince Ali accused Fifa of “blackmail”, saying the governing body had threatened to withhold funds if Jordan refused to back Infantino’s re-election.

“Thank you to the Fifa administration for suddenly this morning delivering what was owed to our players and coaching staff, for the Jordan national team’s accession to the final of the Fifa Arab Cup in Qatar last December,” he wrote.

“This was funding that should have been received eight months ago … It is symptomatic of those exact difficulties that we all face, and that are usually linked to the Fifa presidential elections. And it does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”

Meanwhile on Thursday, the executive committee of the African confederation (Caf) unanimously confirmed its support for Infantino. In a statement it said: “The CAF executive committee unanimously endorses the joint update by the Fifa president and secretary general on the FFE and will continue to focus on making African Football amongst the best in the world and adhering to governance and transparency global best practices.”

Sports.title: Afcon’s biennial switch cost African governing body deal worth more than $1bn
Sports.content:
A deal worth at least $1bn in secured income over eight years was abandoned by the Confederation of African Football (Caf) because the governing body decided to switch the Africa Cup of Nations from a biennial to a four-yearly event, the Guardian can reveal.

On 5 July 2025, the eve of the delayed Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco, the Caf president, Patrice Motsepe, told the Guardian in Rabat, after a prolonged discussion of the bidding process at an executive committee meeting, that a decision on a winning bid would be made “in due course”.

“We announced in Addis Ababa this $1bn partnership that we are looking at over the next eight years. There is a lot of good progress that has been made,” he said.

On 23 July, four days after the World Cup final in New York, Caf opened a fresh tender for the marketing and commercial rights of the 2028, 2032 and 2036 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) tournaments, with bidders given until 24 August to hand in their bid books.

The tender is in complete contrast to the 2025 bidding round, in which the entirety of Caf’s competition portfolio was bundled for sale.

Luxolo September, Caf’s head of communications, confirmed that the change in Afcon frequency is wholly responsible for the abandonment of the 2025 bidding round that was on the verge of completion.

“As foreshadowed by the president in his comments last year, following the receipt and evaluation of bids and presentations from the bidders, in the second half of 2025, Caf entered into detailed discussions with shortlisted bidders regarding the precise terms and conditions of their proposals.

“However, at its meeting on 20 December 2025, the Caf executive committee took a unanimous decision – in the interest of African football – to move the Afcon to a four-year cycle, bringing the competition into alignment with the international match calendar,” September said. “This was a significant decision for African football. That executive committee decision materially changed the scope of the commercial rights available for tender, with the result that the 2025 ITT (Invitation To Tender) process could no longer proceed in its existing form.”

View image in fullscreen Patrice Motsepe (left) said in 2025 that ‘good progress’ was being made over a $1bn deal for Caf. Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty Images

It has been seven years since Caf has had a long-term deal to secure its financial future. The 2016-2028 billion-dollar “minimum guarantee” revenue contract that it signed with the French company Lagardère during the tenure of Issa Hayatou, the late Cameroonian president of Caf, was the first of its kind for the organisation.

“The Memorandum of Understanding with Lagardère was agreed by a team I led with Hicham [El Amrani, then Caf general secretary] in May 2015, in Zurich,” Suketu Patel, then chair of Caf’s finance committee, said in 2019.

“On that same day, we met with Infront. Their indicative offer on the table was a $450m minimum guarantee for eight years, as opposed to the $1bn, for 12 years, from Lagardère.

“If you look at our earlier contract of 2009, we had a minimum guarantee of $150m, but our income for the period was actually around $350m. We anticipated that the 12-year contract would have yielded about $1.3bn.

“I can tell you that whilst President Hayatou and I had differences on political matters, we never had one on the management of Caf finances. He did not interfere with the processes established for good governance.”

But that agreement was unilaterally terminated in December 2019 during the tenure of Ahmad Ahmad, Hayatou’s successor as Caf president.

A protracted legal dispute at the International Chamber of Commerce led to Caf, just over a year into the presidency of Motsepe, paying Lagardère a final settlement of $50m, as compensation for the breach of contract, just before the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

“There is no way that any sponsor will be prepared to pay the same amount of money for a deal in which you would normally have four Afcons over an eight-year period, when you will now only have two. That is certainly a no-brainer,” said a former FA president with expertise in financial matters.

Sports.title: Arsenal hopes dashed after Vinícius Júnior extends Real Madrid contract to 2032
Sports.content:
Vinícius Júnior has ended summer speculation over his future by agreeing a new six-year contract with Real Madrid. Arsenal had been heavily linked with a move for the Brazil international, who had entered the final 12 months of his deal at the Bernabéu.

A tumultuous 2025-26 campaign in which Real failed to win a trophy and initial uncertainty after the arrival of José Mourinho in Madrid alerted the Premier League champions, but Vinícius has now committed his long-term future to the Spanish club.

“Real Madrid and Vinícius Júnior have agreed on the extension of our player’s contract, which links him to the club until 30 June 2032,” a club statement read.

“Vinícius Júnior joined Real Madrid in July 2018 at the age of 18. In his eight seasons wearing our jersey, he has played 375 matches, scored 128 goals, and won 14 titles: two Champions Leagues, three Club World Cups, two Uefa Super Cups, three La Liga titles, one Copa del Rey, and three Spanish Super Cups.

“His contribution to all these titles has been pivotal due to his gameplay, assists, and goals.”

Vinícius wrote on Instagram: “Eight years at the Bernabéu are too few … six more years, and for ever!”

The 26-year-old had hinted at extending his association with Real during an in-house interview on Tuesday where he spoke about Mourinho wanting him to be “happy” and “joyful” after a difficult spell.

A shock last-16 World Cup exit in America with Brazil also added to a frustrating 12-month period for Vinícius, but with his future settled the former Flamengo prospect will aim to help Real get back to competing for major honours again under Mourinho.
