Tying down ‌Vinícius represents another significant ​step in an ​active summer for Real. The club have also strengthened their squad with the arrivals of winger Yan Diomande, midfielder Bernardo Silva, centre-back Ibrahima Konaté, left-back Marc Cucurella and wing-back Denzel Dumfries.

Sports.title: Behind Milburn’s magic: Wor Jackie was a pit village hero and ‘everybody’s friend’ in Newcastle
Sports.content:
Of all the footballers who have worn the black and white, that possessive geordie pronoun “Wor” (our) was unique to Jackie Milburn; for he was a man of the people as much as he was a great sportsman. In that respect, his birthplace of Ashington in Northumberland only added to the mythology.

“The biggest pit village in the world,” as it was known, was the north-east in microcosm – a one-horse coal town where miles of identical terraced houses spread out from the pitheads and the menfolk were obsessed by whippets, leeks, association football and pints in the club. Nevertheless, he had a self-discipline that saw the pitfalls of alcohol: “Certainly it prevented my dad, Alec Milburn, from making the big time,” Jackie recalled. “He could have gone to Tottenham but preferred to stay home and drink his ale.”

At the St James’ Park homecoming following the 1951 FA Cup final, “Wor Jackie” (by which epithet his skipper Joe Harvey introduced him) was invited to address the throng. “At first I tried to ‘talk posh,” Jackie later recalled, “then there was a roar of laughter when a voice shouted, ‘Taak tiv us in your own language, Jackie!’” The dialect of Ashington is one of the most melodious varieties of the ‘pitmatic’ geordie of the coalfields, and still the butt of numerous jokes to this day (when an electrician asked a barmaid where the mains were, the answer came, “Tha just doon there, past the ladies.”)

View image in fullscreen A statue by Tom Maley of Jackie Milburn at Woodhorn Colliery Museum, near Ashington in Northumberland. Photograph: John Angerson/Alamy

Jackie’s lineage was important, for Ashington was an unusually fertile footballing hotbed. His great-grandfather, “Warhorse” Milburn, had kept goal for Northumberland in the 1880s, and young Jackie grew up reading about the Football League exploits of his four Milburn cousins who played professionally, while another cousin, Cissie Charlton, née Milburn, was later almost equally famous as the mother of World Cup winners Jack and Bobby.

Although the coalmines of Ashington demanded their human tribute, professional football was a feasible way out for many – and Milburn once counted 47 local boys he knew of who had played in the First Division. In his 1957 autobiography Golden Goals, he recalled waking early one Christmas morning to find a new pair of football boots at the end of the bed. He slipped them on straight away and headed out into the back lane at half past three in the morning only to find “most of my friends, wearing their new boots, playing football by torchlight in the middle of the street”.

View image in fullscreen Jackie Milburn’s second cousin Bobby Charlton thought that ‘his ball control at speed was as good as anyone I’ve seen’. Photograph: Colorsport/Shutterstock

The prevailing work ethic in pit villages throughout the coalfield helped to mould such formidable players. Miners were famed for their stamina, and with generations of pitmen in his family tree Milburn’s genetics shaped the way he played. In Ashington folklore it was told that Jackie kicked the same stone to school and back for three years, and his one-time teammate Len Shackleton was always impressed by his tenacity and “never-say-die spirit”. This was exemplified by tireless high pressing, and a trademark sliding tackle that hooked the ball from any defender unwise enough to prevaricate on the ball. In his early life he had made money as a sprinter, competing at Edinburgh in the famous Powderhall Handicap and running 100 yards in around 10 seconds.

With his pace, allied to phenomenal shooting power with either foot Milburn rightly takes his place in the Newcastle pantheon. His record of 200 goals in 401 appearances is second only to that of Alan Shearer.

Until 1948 Milburn combined football with work at local collieries, and as he didn’t then have a car, with almost too-perfect symbolism he would take the bus from Ashington into Newcastle with the same supporters who would pay to watch him. “The size of the crowd meant that it sometimes took us up to three-quarters of an hour to walk up the bank and round to the players’ entrance,” Milburn recalled. “But what could we do? Our supporters were a marvellous warm-hearted lot. They even flooded the club with clothing coupons to help kit out the side.” That cosy, close-knit and deeply sociable world of the postwar north-east suited Jackie down to the ground.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle United captain Joe Harvey (c) introduces Prime Minister Winston Churchill (l) to Jackie Milburn (r) before the 1952 FA Cup final. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

“He was everybody’s friend!” wrote his famous second cousin Jack Charlton. “If you ever walked through Newcastle with him, you got stopped every two minutes; everybody said hello to him.”

Yet he never sought this fame, and it’s telling that whenever he went to the pictures in Ashington, he always waited until the lights were down before he entered the auditorium. Here was a modest and even shy man, who shared the small-c conservatism that characterised the otherwise Labour-voting north-east. He was thrilled to meet Winston Churchill at Wembley in 1952 – “the greatest hero of my life whose bust has occupied pride of place in our house since 1948” – as well as the ailing King George VI, whose courage he admired.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle centre forward Jackie Milburn with his wife Laura and daughters Linda (3) and Betty (2) in front of a picture on the wall of Milburn shaking hands with King George VI at the 1951 Cup Final, when his goal won the Cup for Newcastle. Photograph: Mirrorpix/Getty Images

In Golden Goals Milburn presents an image to the world of domestic bliss with his wife, Laura, admitting his aversion to gardening and patterned socks, and his enjoyment of watching TV, reading thrillers and going to the dog track most Wednesdays (greyhounds were always a miners’ passion).

Due to the dominance of a handful of dangerous, heavy industries it was a truism to say that communities across the north-east thrived on being in it together. This may have been one of the reasons why Jackie never quite made a consistent mark on the international stage, despite his 13 caps and 10 goals for England. In later life he confessed that many of his international teammates were too self-obsessed to play as a team and even suggested that “one or two of them were outright snobs”.

View image in fullscreen The Manchester City defenders can only stop and stare as Newcastle United’s Jackie Milburn (left) heads home to score his first-minute goal in the 1955 FA Cup final. Photograph: Popperfoto/Getty Images

Milburn became talismanic for Newcastle. When United’s new manager Dugald Livingstone took the probably rational decision to drop the ageing Milburn for the 1955 FA Cup final against Manchester City on form and fitness grounds, the wily former manager Stan Seymour – by then back upstairs in the boardroom – stepped in to overrule him. Milburn was duly reinstated and would score what was then the fastest Cup final goal – with a rare bullet header from a corner after only 45 seconds.

The people of the area saw in Jackie Milburn the image of their favourite son. He was modest, witty, warm and honest. He was effortlessly, unaffectedly dashing and handsome. He was hard when necessary, but always ready with a grin and a conciliatory word. He was a canny lad with a passion for his homeland.

He was never cautioned in his 14-year career, and the noted First Division whistler Arthur Ellis concluded that: “If there were 22 players on the field like Jackie you wouldn’t need a referee!” His teammate Joe Harvey noted that Jackie was “gentle and generous in victory, always first with the handshake in defeat”, and Milburn himself conceded that his innate courtesy, and tendency to play in colleagues when he had a chance to shoot himself, was a drawback. “I had a lack of devil.”

It’s amazing to think how much more lethal a ruthless Jackie Milburn would have been. But then he probably wouldn’t have been so endearing.

Sports.title: Top Ugandan footballer killed by robbers armed with paving stones
Sports.content:
The Ugandan football community is in mourning after the death of a player who was fatally injured during a robbery in the capital, Kampala, on Tuesday night.

David Owori, who captained Sports Club Villa, a Uganda Premier League club, and represented the national team, was attacked after resisting an attempt to steal his mobile phone and other belongings near his home in Makindye division.

Racheal Kawala, a spokesperson for the Kampala Metropolitan police, said he was found unconscious by ​passersby, who took him to a nearby hospital. He was ​transferred to another hospital, where he was pronounced dead on Wednesday.

Witnesses said attackers hit the footballer with paving stones before robbing him and fleeing, leaving him unconscious, the BBC reported.

Owori, 27, was a right-back and midfielder for SC Villa. He helped the team win a record 17th Uganda Premier League title in 2024.

He started his senior career in 2016 at the Uganda Premier League side Vipers Sports Club and had stints in Europe with Vélez CF in Spain and Utsiktens BK in Sweden.

He played for the national team in the qualifiers for the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations.

SC Villa said: “It is with profound sorrow that we announce the untimely passing of our captain, Owori, who had been receiving treatment at Case Clinic following an attack by suspected thugs. Our deepest condolences and prayers are with his family.”

The Federation ​of Uganda Football Associations said: “David was not just a footballer. He was ​both a leader and an inspiration to a generation. As ​Captain of SC Villa, he led with courage, humility and passion. In the Uganda Cranes jersey, he carried the hopes of a nation.”

It added: “We have lost a son, a leader and a star. His light on and off the pitch will never be forgotten.”

The Ugandan parliament observed a minute of silence in Owori’s honour on Wednesday.

In June Sydney Gongodyo, a Ugandan rugby international, ​died after a mob attacked him in Kampala, mistaking him for a thief, police said.

Uganda’s National Council of Sports said: “Sadly, ​Ugandan sport has been hit with many such ​tragedies lately, and we hope for justice and a lasting solution.”

Sports.title: Kerolin failed to report for pre-season at Manchester City before Barcelona switch
Sports.content:
The Brazil forward Kerolin failed to report back for pre-season training at Manchester City in July before her transfer to Barcelona had been agreed.

Barcelona announced their signing of the 26-year-old on Tuesday but it was not until Thursday evening when Manchester City first made any reference to the transfer, eventually confirming they had received a WSL record fee for a sale more than 48 hours later.

Several staff and players at Manchester City were disappointed at what were perceived to be efforts by Kerolin to force a transfer to Barcelona and that her time at the club ended on a surprisingly sour note. She did not join pre-season with the Women’s Super League champions, which began in late July, despite previously having been felt to have been on good terms with the squad.

The deal, worth an initial €1.2m (£1m), represents the largest transfer fee received by a WSL club, and it could rise with add-ons to approximately £1.25m, although this has not been officially confirmed. It is one of the largest transfer fees in women’s football.

City said of Kerolin: “She grabbed 14 goals and six assists during that time, helping City to a WSL and FA Cup double in her solitary full season in England. And upon her transfer to Barça, City have received a WSL-club record transfer fee of €1.2m.

“Everyone at Manchester City would like to thank Kerolin for all her efforts at the club and wish her the very best in her future career.”

Kerolin was part of the City side that lifted their first WSL title in a decade last season and also helped them win the Women’s FA Cup. But within weeks of those celebrations many of her City colleagues have been stunned after she did not say goodbye in-person. Kerolin’s representatives have been contacted for a response.

High-profile examples of such transfer standoffs have been seen in men’s football, but incidents in the women’s game have been comparatively rare.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

City have no objections to the transfer in principle but sources have said the team were taken aback by the former North Carolina Courage star’s absence from pre-season fitness testing. For Kerolin, it is a dream move to the European champions, who beat OL Lyonnes in last season’s Women’s Champions League final.

City and Barcelona will meet in a friendly at the Joie Stadium on 15 August as the reigning champions of England and Spain step up their pre-season preparations.

Sports.title: Barcelona step up Rodri interest after Real Madrid talks with Manchester City star stall
Sports.content:
Barcelona have stepped up their attempts to hijack Real Madrid’s move to sign Rodri from Manchester City.

While City have not given up hope that Spain’s World Cup-winning captain will sign a new contract after he entered the final year of his deal, they are thought to be willing to allow him to leave for about £60m. Despite weeks of talks with Rodri and his representatives, Real have yet to reach an agreement and Barcelona are hoping to take advantage.

It is understood that Rodri spoke to their manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director, Deco, about a potential move on Wednesday and indicated he is keen to return to Spain. Barça, who will be without midfielder Frenkie de Jong for several months after the Netherlands midfielder sustained a knee injury, are now expected to make contact with City to negotiate the structure of the fee for the 30-year-old, who won the Golden Ball for the World Cup’s best player.

Real, who have signed RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande for a club record fee of £115m, have also agreed a lucrative six-year contract extension with Vinícius Júnior to ward off interest from Arsenal. They may have to offload players first if they are to sign Rodri as well. Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga are possible departures, with Manchester United having been linked with the France midfielders.

Rodri has had minor surgery on his back and will miss most of City’s pre-season programme. They have signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and remain in negotiations with Lille over a deal for the 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Meanwhile, Barcelona have been frustrated in their efforts to persuade Atlético Madrid to sell Julián Alvarez. After Robert Lewandowski’s departure, Barcelona have targeted Alvarez all summer, but Atlético continue to insist the Argentina striker is not for sale at any price.

Deco was in the Spanish capital to meet Alvarez’s representatives on Wednesday. All eyes will be on whether the 26-year-old former City forward will return to pre-season training on Monday or attempt to force through a transfer. Arsenal also retain an interest in him.

Ferran Torres – who scored the winning goal for Spain in the World Cup final against Argentina – has entered the final year of his contract at Barcelona and said he is waiting for them to begin talks over extending his deal. “All I know is that I have to be in training for Barcelona on 12 August. Let’s see what happens.” Asked what Barcelona needed to do to keep him, he said: “Show me they want me, come to negotiate.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Meanwhile, James Trafford sealed a club-record move to Leeds after completing a medical at Elland Road. Leeds have agreed a £40m fee plus add-ons with City for the 23-year-old, who will become the world’s fourth most expensive goalkeeper.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah to earn upwards of £14.5m per season in two-year Trabzonspor deal
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah has signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor and the Egypt forward will receive €17m (£14.5m) a season.

The ⁠announcement to ‌the Turkish stock ‌exchange came ​as Trabzonspor fans prepared to head to the club’s stadium for a ceremony to mark the 34-year-old’s former Liverpool player’s signing on a free transfer the day after ⁠Salah arrived in Istanbul in the team’s kit.

Thousands of supporters cheered in Trabzonspor’s stadium, waving club flags, holding torches and chanting songs.

At his signing ceremony, Salah said: “The last couple of days, it’s an experience I’ve ⁠never had in my life. I just want to thank every one of you ​for being here today. I am ‌feeling so much love ‌here I never expected that reception.

“I ‌am here to win, I want to win something with this club because you showed me so much love – I appreciate that.”

Salah will receive a 20% share from products sold ‌under his name, plus conditional bonuses each season.

View image in fullscreen Mohamed Salah takes photos of the scenes in the stands after his first taste of life as one of Papara Park’s own. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters

Salah left Liverpool after nine years, having scored 257 goals in 442 appearances, winning the Premier League twice and the Champions League. His output waned last season and he was left ​on the bench in European games, leading to a public disagreement with Liverpool’s then manager Arne Slot.

Trabzonspor – generally considered to ​be the fourth-biggest team in Turkey after Fenerbahce, Galatasaray and ‌Besiktas – finished ​third in the ​Super Lig last season to qualify for the Europa League playoff round. They last won the league title in 2022.

Sports.title: Rodri’s decision made public in Barcelona vs Real Madrid transfer race
Sports.content:
Rodri has told Barcelona he wants to join them this summer, his agent has revealed.

Real Madrid recently opened talks with City over a move for the World Cup winning Spain captain.

2 Fresh from winning the World Cup, Rodri finds himself at the centre of a high-profile transfer battle Credit: Getty

However, their famous arch rivals have swooped in to hijack the deal.

talkSPORT reported on Thursday that Barca had moved ahead of Madrid in the race to sign Rodri.

Now, the 30-year-old's agent Pablo Barquero has told Spanish TV that his client is prioritising a move to the Nou Camp.

“Out of respect for Madrid, as they have been class, Rodri informed them that his decision is to join Barca," Barquero said.

Rodri is out of contract at the Etihad next summer, but City are still thought to be demanding a significant transfer fee, more than the £42million being reported.

City are not yet resigned to losing Rodri this summer and could elect to keep the four-time Premier League winner - even if he refuses to sign a new deal.

The midfielder, who won the Ballon d'Or in 2024 and the Golden Ball at the 2026 World Cup, is thought to prefer a move to Spain due to family reasons.

Rodri is expected to be sidelined for the beginning of the season, wherever that may be, after recently undergoing back surgery.

Keep at all costs?

City recently signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and are expected to land superstar Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

However, talkSPORT host Adam Catterall recently argued that losing Rodri could cost City their shot at regaining the Premier League title.

2 Anderson is City's latest big-money signing Credit: Isaac Parkin / Manchester City FC

"There's a lot of chat about Rodri, at the moment, off the back of his fantastic World Cup (with Spain)," he said.

"I know that off the back of his injury last year, he wasn't at his scintillating best, but the World Cup kind of pointed in the direction that the Ballon d'Or winner is back to his very, very best.

"I genuinely believe that if he does go to Real Madrid in this window, that will scupper any chances that Manchester City have of winning the Premier League.

"I think he's that influential. He has to be at City, if City are going to make a Premier League challenge this year."

Ex-Premier League defender Ashley Williams added: "My concern is that they've brought in Elliot Anderson and think, 'We can probably live without Rodri', but they can't, I think they need both of them.

"I love Elliot Anderson, I think he's brilliant, he'll be the future.

"But wouldn't it be great for him to have all that he's got already and learn off Rodri with the way he plays? And have both of them at least overlapping for a couple of seasons.

"At no point would you ever, ever get rid of Rodri, for no amount of money. They could offer me whatever and I wouldn't sell Rodri."

Sports.title: ‘We’ll be laughing’ – Tottenham told to let Arsenal sign star in unthinkable transfer
Sports.content:
‘We’ll be laughing’ – Tottenham told to let Arsenal sign star in unthinkable transfer

Tottenham Hotspur have been urged to let bitter rivals Arsenal sign Cristian Romero this summer.

The Gunners have emerged as surprise candidates to land the Spurs captain ahead of the new season.



3 Spurs have been told to allow Romero to join bitter rivals Arsenal Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta's side are reported to have shown interest in Romero, who is likely to leave Tottenham before the transfer window closes.

According to The Athletic, Arsenal have joined Atletico Madrid in eyeing the Argentina defender.

Italian champions Inter Milan are also in contention for the 28-year-old's signature.



The Serie A giants' sporting director confirmed last month that talks had been held.

Arsenal's desire to sign a new centre-back comes with William Saliba sidelined for the foreseeable future.



Saliba suffered a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain.

'Let them have him'

Spurs fan and former Premier League player Darren Ambrose has now told his club to let Romero join Arsenal.



Reacting to the news alongside Majestic on The Sports Bar, the talkSPORT co-host said: "Let them have him… liability. Give Micky van de Ven the captaincy."

Ambrose continued: "Surely they wouldn't, he's got a contract until 2029 so he won't be cheap.

"It's different to the Sol Campbell situation. If they want him they have to pay big money to get him and then we'll be laughing when he loses them every couple of games with a red card."

3 Spurs fans will be 'laughing' if Arsenal sign Romero, says Ambrose Credit: Getty



Romero signed a new four-year deal through to the summer of 2029 in August last year.

However, a second-successive 17th place finish in the Premier League has seen talk of a departure resurface this summer.

It follows a season marred by ill-discipline for the World Cup winner.

Romero was sent off twice in 23 league appearances last term as well as receiving ten yellow cards.



Since joining Spurs in 2021, he has been shown six red cards across all competitions.

Van de Ven latest

Whilst Romero could leave Spurs before the window closes, Micky van de Ven appears set to stay at the club.

3 Whilst Romero may leave, Van de Ven is expected to sign a new Spurs contract Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands the defender is expected to sign a new deal following positive discussions.



Manager Roberto De Zerbi has played a key role in convincing the 25-year-old to commit his future to the club.

Meanwhile, Van de Ven's priority has been to extend his stay since Spurs achieved Premier League survival in May.

Talks have since accelerated, with the club hopeful an agreement will be finalised this month.

Sports.title: Man United announce signing of South American wonderkid, 18
Sports.content:
Add us as preferred source

Manchester United have announced the signing of 18-year-old Cristian Orozco.

The teenage midfielder has joined the Red Devils from Fortaleza CEIF in his native Colombia.



3 United have confirmed the signing of teenage midfielder Orozco Credit: Getty

It comes after United agreed a deal to sign Orozco back in September.

He has now officially arrived at Old Trafford after turning 18 last month.

Previous United signing Diego Leon saw his move delayed in similar fashion last summer before joining from Cerro Porteno.

Orozco featured five times for Fortaleza's first-team last season.

He will initially be part of the club's academy having already featured for the under-21s against Altrincham last week.



The youngster becomes Michael Carrick's sixth signing of the summer.

Orozco follows fellow prospects Tynan Thompson and Kit Margetson through the door.

Meanwhile, the United first-team has also been strengthened by the arrivals of Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow.



The Red Devils will return to the Champions League this season following their third place finish last term.

Who is Cristian Orozco?

Orozco has been capped by Colombia up to under-17 level so far in his international career.



3 Orozco has already made his under-21s debut and will join up with the club's academy Credit: Getty

He was also part of their squad for last year's South American U17 Championship.

Colombia reached the final on home soil before losing to Brazil on penalties.

Orozco later captained the side at the U17 World Cup in Qatar in November.



They were unable to replicate their previous success, though, losing to France in the round of 32.

His arrival at United sees Orozco become the club's third ever Colombian player.

He follows in the footsteps of Radamel Falcao and Mateo Mejia by joining the Red Devils.

3 Orozco captained Colombia at last year's U17 World Cup in Qatar Credit: Getty



Falcao spent the 2014/15 season on loan at United, scoring four goals in 26 Premier League appearances.

Meanwhile, Mejia featured for the club's under-21 side in the EFL Trophy during five years on their books.

Sports.title: Barcelona forced to cancel pre-season friendly as statement given
Sports.content:
Barcelona forced to cancel pre-season friendly as statement given

Barcelona have postponed a pre-season friendly match in Morocco later this month.

The Spanish giants cited 'uncertainty and circumstances' for their decision to cancel the match.

3 Barcelona have cancelled their planned pre-season friendly in Morocco on August 15 Credit: Getty

Hansi Flick's side had been due to continue their preparations for the new season in Tangier on Saturday, August 15.

It is understood Moroccan top-flight outfit IR Tangier would have been their opponents.

The club play at the 75,000-capacity Tangier Grand Stadium which was renovated for last year's Africa Cup of Nations.

However, they will no longer face Barcelona at the venue later this month.

Barcelona statement

In a statement, Barca said: "FC Barcelona informs that the men's first team friendly match in Tangier potentially scheduled for 15 August has been ruled out.

"In light of the current uncertainty and circumstances, FC Barcelona considers playing the match would be inappropriate."

It is not the first pre-season fixture which the LaLiga champions have had cancelled this summer.

During their recent trip to England, Barca were scheduled to face Preston North End in a behind-closed-doors contest on Monday.

The match was ultimately called off after the Championship side offered to field an Under-21 XI instead.

Preston were reported to have not wanted to risk any injuries to their first-team squad in the fixture.

3 Barcelona cited 'uncertainty and circumstances' as they postponed their match at Tangier Grand Stadium Credit: Getty

Barcelona also faced Birmingham City at St. Andrew's during their training camp in England.

The match ended in a 2-2 draw before Blues won the subsequent penalty shootout 3-2.

Barca will continue their summer schedule at the Venezia Giulia Cup this weekend.

They will face both Nottingham Forest and Udinese on Saturday as part of the friendly tournament.

Both matches are set to last 45 minutes and are being played at Udinese's Stadio Friuli.

Barca will then conclude their pre-season campaign at home to Egyptian side Al Ahly on August 19.

3 Barca return to pre-season action with matches against Forest and Udinese on Saturday Credit: Getty

That match comes just four days before they begin their LaLiga title defence.

Their opening fixture of the season sees them face Elche away from home.

Sports.title: Only one Premier League club is big enough to sign Vinicius Jr and it’s not Arsenal
Sports.content:
Only one Premier League club is big enough to sign Vinicius Jr and it’s not Arsenal

Arsenal have been told they are not a big enough brand to be able to sign Vinicius Jr this summer.

The Gunners presented a pitch to the Real Madrid forward in a bid to convince him to join the club, although he's decided to sign a new six-year deal with the Spanish giants.



4 Arteta and Arsenal have been handed a reality check in their pursuit of Vinicius Jr Credit: Getty

But there was uncertainty surrounding his long-term future at the Santiago Bernabeu. Vinicius Jr was in the final year of his previous contract this summer.

Productive talks were held with the player on Wednesday following Arsenal's own offer of personal terms.

The Premier League champions were prepared to move for Vinicius Jr this summer if didn't extend his stay at Real Madrid.



'Only one club can sign Vinicius Jr'

talkSPORT's Adam Catterall believes only one Premier League club would have the capacity to land the 26-year-old, though.

Notably, that club is not Arsenal, with Catterall instead naming Manchester United as the one side capable of doing so.



Discussing Arsenal's interest alongside Carlton Cole, he explained earlier on Thursday: "For me, when you’re talking about brands, and when you’re talking about being able to attract the biggest, and that’s what he is, he is a brand.

"Listen, he’s a sensational footballer, but he’s a brand as well, being able to attract him to you.



"For me, there’s only one football club in the whole of the United Kingdom that could attract someone like Vinicius Jr. There’s one.

4 Real Madrid are confident Vinicius Jr will sign a new deal after productive talks Credit: Getty

"There’s only Manchester United as a brand that could attract him and people will come at me and say, ‘well, what about Manchester City?’

"City are around what? About 55 million, 56 million (followers)? Something like that on Instagram? Look at Real Madrid.



"This is the point Gabby (Agbonlahor) was making this morning. I know that he was making it regarding trophies and what have you, but look at the brand value."

Gabby Agbonlahor labelled Arsenal fans 'deluded' for thinking they could sign Vinicius Jr on talkSPORT Breakfast earlier on Thursday morning.

The former Aston Villa striker even compared their hopes of doing the deal to himself inviting music superstar Rihanna to Birmingham for a date.

Market manipulation

When informed Real Madrid have 180 million Instagram followers, Catterall continued: "There you go. That’s how big that football club is. That’s how big that is as a worldwide entity.



4 Catterall believes Arsenal are not a big enough brand to sign Vinicius Jr Credit: talkSPORT

"180 million and you’re talking about him coming to a club that has 32 million followers on Instagram.

"Again, these are very basic metrics, very basic metrics, but Vinicius Jr is in a completely different stratosphere.

"All this talk about him coming to Arsenal throughout the whole course of the summer has just been manipulation from an agent trying to get the dude a few more quid. That’s what it is.



"He was never in a million years going to be an Arsenal player this summer. That’s what it is. It’s just manipulating the market.

"Let’s see if I can get some more money for my guy. Why would he come to Arsenal?"

At the time of writing, Arsenal have 32.3 million Instagram followers to their name.

4 United are the only Premier League club big enough to sign Vinicius Jr, says Catterall Credit: Getty



Mikel Arteta's side are fresh from winning their first Premier League title for 22 years last season.

The Gunners also reached the Champions League final, but lost on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest.

Sports.title: James Trafford becomes Leeds’ highest-paid player as record-breaking deal announced
Sports.content:
James Trafford has started the journey to becoming England's future No.1 by sealing his record-breaking transfer to Leeds United.

He has now signed a five-year deal at Elland Road to become Leeds' highest-paid player, banking eye-watering wages of £170,000-a-week.

3 Trafford has completed a permanent move to Leeds, becoming their highest-paid player Credit: Getty

Leeds will pay a club-record fee for Trafford of £40m, plus add-ons. This eclipses the £36m they paid to sign Georginio Rutter in 2023.

The 23-year-old, who was an unused back-up to Jordan Pickford at the World Cup, has officially left Manchester City for a second time.

Trafford had been keen to leave City in search of a No.1 job at another Premier League club, as previously revealed by talkSPORT.

The goalkeeper, a former Newcastle target, played just 17 times after returning to his boyhood club from Burnley last summer.

Trafford rejoined the Etihad set-up last summer in a £27million deal - just two years after Pep Guardiola sanctioned his £14m exit.

He started in the opening three Premier League games of the season, but City's deadline-day swoop for Gianluigi Donnarumma relegated him to a No.2 role for the remainder of the 2025/26 season.

Trafford ultimately made only one more top-flight appearance under Pep Guardiola, but kept eight clean sheets across all competitions to help the club claim a domestic double.

Upon sealing his departure from City, Trafford said in an emotional message to fans: "To everyone at Man City, it was my dream to play for the first team from when I moved away from home at 12.

"And it makes me so proud to have achieved that last season, whilst also winning two trophies in the process.

"The fans singing my name was something I dreamt of when I went to the Etihad growing up through the academy.

3 Trafford won two trophies last season with Man City Credit: Getty

"I wish nothing but the best for the club for the future."

Leeds get their man

Upon signing for Leeds, Trafford captioned a social media post which showed a picture of him signing the contract: "Marching on together, let’s do something special."

Whites boss Daniel Farke was in desperate need of reinforcements between the sticks following a flurry of exits in that department.

Illan Meslier and Karl Darlow have already both left Leeds this summer, to back-up roles at Arsenal and Man United respectively.

Meanwhile, Brazilian shot-stopper Lucas Perri is closing in on a switch to Italian outfit Torino.

Trafford is a two-cap England international and was part of the squad at this summer's World Cup.

3 Trafford is in good company in terms of expensive Premier League goalkeepers

Arguably the best achievement of the 23-year-old's career so far saw him help England win the Under-21 European Championship in 2023.

He proved to be the hero having saved a last-minute penalty to seal the Young Lions a 1-0 win over Spain.

Sports.title: How Enzo Maresca and Hugo Viana created the new Man City with two-year post-Guardiola plan - the four 'cornerstone' players set to fill leadership void and who's coming and going in midfield overhaul
Sports.content:
How Enzo Maresca and Hugo Viana created the new Man City with two-year post-Guardiola plan - the four 'cornerstone' players set to fill leadership void and who's coming and going in midfield overhaul

Unlock more from Jack Gaughan inside the Man City camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

There has been an obvious drive over the summer to futureproof the Manchester City squad, with Jeremy Doku becoming the latest star to commit to a new five-year contract.

Doku joins Josko Gvardiol, Phil Foden and Abdukodir Khusanov in agreeing fresh terms over the past fortnight, the quartet seen as integral to the new era of City. A City without Pep Guardiola and a City without so many of the stalwarts synonymous with rampant success.

Gvardiol and Doku, two of last season’s standout performers, are still only 24 (Foden is 26, Khusanov 22) and the hope is that the pair are the sort of figures who will provide a cornerstone to an evolving team and club.

Clearly, director of football Hugo Viana and new boss Enzo Maresca have identified the men they believe can step into the shoes of Bernardo Silva, Kevin De Bruyne, Riyad Mahrez and more than a few others in exacting standards and taking on the responsibility of delivering consistent trophies.

It is difficult to think of too many harder jobs in elite football than that right now, especially if Rodri secures a move back to Spain, with Barcelona now rivalling Real Madrid for his signature.

A departure of a midfielder crowned the best player at the World Cup would leave City’s four-man leadership group cut in half in recent months and points to the lack of real experience – something Maresca addressed earlier in the stifling week in Seoul.

Jeremy Doku (left) has become the latest Manchester City star to commit to a new five-year contract

Defender Josko Gvardiol has also agreed fresh terms, and is a key part of the City rebuild under Enzo Maresca

Rodri will leave very large boots to fill should he leave for Barcelona or Real Madrid

Gvardiol and Foden have both publicly raised their hands to take roles in the captaincy team and there is jostling behind the scenes between players who want to make their mark under a fresh regime – one that ought to offer some of them renewed energy.

Nico Gonzalez, who failed to start a single league game between January and May, insisted that he is one of them.

‘I’m happy here,’ said Gonzalez, who joined for £50million 18 months ago. ‘I don’t want to leave and I think the club wants me to stay. If we win, I’m happy. My dream is to win trophies.

'If I don’t play any matches and we win the Champions League next year, I will be so happy. The final of the FA Cup I was not picked but we won so it was an amazing day for me. To be honest, last season I couldn’t have expected to have played almost 30 matches in the starting XI. I played really good. I’ve had many opportunities.’

Gonzalez – who didn’t even make the bench for that FA Cup final he referenced – does have his price but it has become clearer in recent days that Tijjani Reijnders is more likely to exit the building before the window closes. Nottingham Forest and Newcastle United are monitoring the Dutchman, valued at £55million.

Be it Rodri or Reijnders or both, City sources have indicated that they are ready to replace any potential outgoings. The pursuit of Ayyoub Bouaddi, a breakout talent at the World Cup with Morocco, is a separate entity and they are pressing ahead with negotiations with Lille regardless of movements in the other direction.

They had accelerated the rebuild in January, spending £85million on Antoine Semenyo and Marc Guehi, with the two signings from Bournemouth and Crystal Palace embedded into the squad then rather than now – which ought to represent something of an advantage moving forward.

Semenyo contributed to two trophy wins – scoring the FA Cup-winning goal over Chelsea – while Guehi was ineligible to feature in the Carabao Cup final, a decision that riled Guardiola.

Nico Gonzalez insists he is happy at City despite failing to start a league game between January and May

City are pressing ahead with negotiations with Lille for Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi (right)

But Tijjani Reijnders could be on the way out amid interest from Nottingham Forest and Newcastle

City believe the strategy of doing those deals six months early, and supplementing it by breaking their transfer record with £116million Elliot Anderson once Maresca assumed the post, will reap its rewards.

‘I don’t think any player has the position guaranteed for all the matches,’ Gonzalez added. ‘We are one of the best teams in the world and obviously there is competition in every position. That is what makes us be in the position that we are, winning so many Premier Leagues and competing for everything.’

Gonzalez is talking about a different squad though. He’s never won a title. Only five of this group were around for the Treble, revealing quite how much rebuilding has gone on in the three seasons since.

City have spent much of the last two years planning for this moment, for life after Guardiola, and now the time has come to determine how meticulous that has been.

Sports.title: Roy Keane and Micah Richards dress up as traditional Victorian gentlemen, perform pigskin keepy-uppies and enjoy a day out at the terraces as they turn back the clock for Sky Bet's new 'Game's Back' campaign
Sports.content:
Roy Keane and Micah Richards dress up as traditional Victorian gentlemen, perform pigskin keepy-uppies and enjoy a day out at the terraces as they turn back the clock for Sky Bet's new 'Game's Back' campaign

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roy Keane and Micah Richards have embraced football's roots by dressing as Victorian gentlemen for Sky Bet's latest 'Game's Back' campaign.

Revisiting football's earliest days ahead of the new Premier League season, the popular Sky Sports punditry duo donned period costumes as they took in the action from the terraces and showed off their keepy-uppy skills with a traditional pigskin ball.

Sky Bet's new campaign, which is officially launching on August 7, plays on the familiar 'game's gone' phrase often used by supporters looking back nostalgically at how the sport has changed over the years, from players refusing to celebrate against former clubs to the introduction of VAR.

In one light-hearted moment, Richards dares to shush his famously fiery punditry partner while the pair watch on from the stands, poking fun at Keane's well-known habit of questioning changes in the modern game.

Sky Bet's campaign sees Keane and Richards embark on a journey through football's past, revisiting different eras of the sport to highlight that debates over change have existed ever since the game's earliest era.

Their trip begins in Victorian times, where the pair witness the birth of modern football and discover that supporters were already questioning how the game was evolving.

Popular punditry duo Roy Keane and Micah Richards have embraced football's roots by dressing as Victorian gentlemen for Sky Bet's latest 'Game's Back' campaign

Sky Bet's new campaign plays on the familiar 'the game's gone' phrase often used by supporters looking back nostalgically at how the sport has changed over the years

Richards and Keane also showed off their keepy-uppy skills with a traditional pigskin ball

Keane said: 'One thing about football history is that people have always questioned changes to the game, but it's funny looking back at some of the things we'd never want to lose now.

'We had good fun bringing those moments to life.'

Richards added: 'Football fans love a debate and that's never going to change'.

'Game's Gone is a phrase that has engrained itself in football culture and beyond,' said Harry Phillips, Sky Bet Marketing Director.

'Yet even though we all love to moan about the game, it's never been more universally popular and when push comes to shove, it's the incredible moments of football culture, both on and off the pitch that keeps us coming back.

'We believe football always has and always will create moments no fan can resist. And at Sky Bet, we champion those iconic moments of football and fandom by giving our customers more ways to get in on the action.'

The new Premier League season kicks off with champions Arsenal hosting newly-promoted Coventry City on Friday, August 21.

Sports.title: Man City target new goalkeeper after James Trafford sale, Bruno Guimaraes nears £75m Arsenal move and Man United confirm signing of star, 18: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man City target new goalkeeper after James Trafford sale, Bruno Guimaraes nears £75m Arsenal move and Man United confirm signing of star, 18: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Arsenal interested in Spurs captain

Arsenal admire Cristian Romero - but a sale to the Gunners would not be contemplated by Tottenham.

The Spurs captain remains the subject of strong interest from Atletico Madrid and Inter who had a £34.2m fee in place.

Spurs meanwhile are preparing a new long-term contract for defender Micky van de Ven.

The Netherlands centre-back has a deal until 2029.

Spurs defender Ashley Phillips is joining Middlesbrough for £7m and the deal could rise to £20m with bonuses. Spurs have also negotiated a 20 per cent sell-on clause and matching rights into the transfer agreement.

Real get their Diomande

Real Madrid have reached an agreement with RB Leipzig to sign one-time Liverpool target Yan Diomande on a seven-year contract.

Real are paying a guaranteed fee of £107million for the 19-year-old, with the total deal worth up to £120m.

Yan Diomande - who was a target for Liverpool earlier this summer - has joined Real Madrid

Liverpool had an offer worth £85m rejected earlier in the window while PSG also tried to sign the Ivory Coast international. Diomande scored 13 goals and provided 10 assists in 36 appearances last season.

Liverpool are currently working to add PSG pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Nestory time at Sporting

Sporting Lisbon have agreed a deal worth around £17m for Watford forward Nestory Irankunda.

Bayern Munich have a 40 per cent sell-on clause for the Australia international and will be due around £7m.

Diomande in doubt

Ousmane Diomande's move to Nottingham Forest has hit a major snag with the deal now far from certain.

Forest had been close to agreeing a fee of about £35m with Sporting Lisbon for the centre-back but Daily Mail Sport understands talks have hit the buffers.

Oliver Glasner had made the centre-back his top target - as he did at Crystal Palace last summer, which also proved unsuccessful.

Ousmane Diomande's move to Nottingham Forest is understood to have hit a snag

It now remains to be seen if the transfer can be revived in the remaining days of the window.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Trafford completes Leeds switch

James Trafford has completed a move from Manchester City to Leeds in a deal that could reach £45m.

Trafford becomes the most expensive English goalkeeper of all time after the clubs struck an agreement on £40m plus £5m in add-ons.

Man City are closing on agreement with Marseille for goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli.

The 34-year-old will cost around £2.9million and will replace Trafford.

The deal will allow Lucas Perri to move from Leeds to Torino. The Italians are waiting for Perri to recover from a small injury which kept him out of Leeds' last two pre-season games before finalising the move.

Leeds have a list of around five goalkeepers as they plot their search for Trafford's deputy.

They have Alex Cairns but want another to cover Perri's departure too.

San Lorenzo's Paraguay international Orlando Gill is one but they are yet to make an offer.

Dykes snubs Charlton for Millwall

Scotland striker Lyndon Dykes has agreed a one-year deal with Millwall.

The 30-year-old has completed a medical and is finalising his move.

Dykes rejected a longer term offer from Charlton Athletic, where he spent the second half of last season, as he looks to help Millwall earn promotion.

Scotland forward Lyndon Dykes is set to join Millwall

Villa and Toon keep tabs on defender

Racing Santander defender Jorge Salinas is attracting attention from Aston Villa and Newcastle United.

The 19-year-old can play left back and centre back and has also been watched by Barcelona and Manchester United scouts.

Some of the clubs view him as a player for the future while others are considering a bid this month.

Bruno heads to the capital

Bruno Guimaraes is understood to be in London to finalise his £75million move to Arsenal.

The 28-year-old left Newcastle's pre-season camp on Wednesday after a fee of £75m was agreed with Arsenal. Newcastle are continuing to work on a replacement.

Napoli have enquired about striker Gabriel Jesus at Arsenal.

Bruno Guimaraes is in London to complete his move from Newcastle to Arsenal

Gunners keep tabs on the next Kvaratskhelia

Arsenal scouts were at Larne's Europa League qualifier against Iberia 1999 on Tuesday.

They were understood to be running the rule over the Georgian side's attacking midfielder Andria Bartishvili.

The exciting 17-year-old has been on Arsenal's radar for a number of months and has been compared in style to compatriot Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at Paris St Germain.

Indeed, the French side are also understood to be among his admirers as well as clubs in Italy.

Bartishvili is on loan at Iberia from Kolkheti 1913, however, he is expected to be sold in the coming days as interest intensifies.

Hammers confirm Veltman

West Ham have confirmed the signing of former Brighton defender Joel Veltman.

The Dutch defender has signed a one-year contract with an option for a second year.

'I'm delighted to have signed, and I can't wait to get started,' said Veltman. 'The project here really excites me.'

'I spoke to Nuno [Espírito Santo], as well as my family and my agent, and everything added up. We know that West Ham need to be in the Premier League, and for sure that is our goal for the season.

'I think I bring my experience, my winning mentality and togetherness. I bring leadership - I've been the captain at Ajax, and I enjoy talking to my teammates and using my experience to help the squad.

'I'm just so excited to give everything, to meet my new teammates and to see all the supporters too.'

West Ham are also prepared to break the Championship transfer record of £17.5m to sign Troy Parrott from AZ Alkmaar. Talks have opened between the clubs.

Talks for Spurs winger Manor Solomon are currently off over bonus payments.

West Ham have announced the signing of Brighton defender Joel Veltman

JOEL VELTMAN STATS Played 24 Premier League matches in 25-26, but only started nine and played 1050 minutes Scored once last season - against West Ham (2-2 draw at London Stadium to salvage a point for Brighton) Across the Premier League season, Veltman made a total of 99 defensive contributions Won 75 duels (67% success rate) Won 20 aerial duels (62.5% success rate) 31 tackles 18 interceptions Six shots blocked 10 fouls committed 40 recoveries 44 clearances Five yellow cards Started all four cup matches he played in (two in Carabao Cup, two in FA Cup) *By Isabelle Martin

Barca rival Real Madrid's interest in Rodri

Barcelona have finally made their interest in Manchester City midfielder Rodri official to rival Real Madrid for his signature.

Rodri wants to return to Spain but Manchester City have been waiting for other clubs to declare their interest to get the optimum price for the 30-year-old.

Barcelona have finally expressed their interest in Manchester City and Spain midfielder Rodri

They have made a new contract offer to the Spain captain who has one year left but are aware of his desire to explore a move back.

Rodri was keen on a move to Madrid but equally is understood to be open to joining Barca's project where eight of the national team are in the current squad.

Sanchez joins Cherries

Bournemouth have announced the signing of right-back Juanlu Sanchez, 22, from Sevilla in a deal worth £11.2m.

Man United's newest signing

Man United have signed 18-year-old midfielder Cristian Orozco from Colombian side Fortaleza CEIF for their U21s.

Boro agree deal for Phillips

Tottenham and Middlesbrough have agreed a £7million deal plus add ons for centre back Ashley Phillips.

The 21-year-old's former club Blackburn are due a sell on percentage.

A central defender became Boro's priority after Dael Fry's decision to leave for Birmingham at the end of his contract.

Munoz reports for duty

Spain winger Victor Munoz reported to Liverpool training for the first time yesterday following his £34.5million move from Osasuna.

Munoz moved to Los Rojillos last summer from Real Madrid, for whom he made four appearances after graduating from their youth set-up having previously been with the academy of his hometown club, Barcelona.

Munoz was the first new addition after the arrival of head coach Andoni Iraola.

Victor Munoz with agents Juanma Lopez and Andy Bara from Niagara Sports

And Chambers could head to Championship

Liverpool left-back Luke Chambers is attracting interest from QPR, Blackburn Rovers and others.

The 22-year-old has impressed during Liverpool's pre-season and has drawn several enquiries including another from a European club and one more Championship side.

The former England U20 international has previously been on loan at Kilmarnock, Wigan Athletic and Charlton Athletic.

Saints teen heads to Italy

Southampton winger Jay Robinson arrived in Milan's Linate airport at 9pm last night ahead of sealing his loan move to newly-promoted Serie A side Monza.

The 19-year-old, who made his Premier League debut in 2025, made 23 appearances in the Championship last season but his campaign was hindered by a quad injury.

The teenager, who has also represented England at every age group from U16s up to the U19s, is hoping to gain regular game time in Italy's top flight.

Southampton winger Jay Robinson is set to seal a loan move to Serie A club Monza

Celtic have made a £6m bid for Real Oviedo’s Egyptian winger Haissem Hassan. The fee could rise to £9m if all bonuses are achieved.

Ipswich Town are in advanced talks with Fulham over the signing of midfielder Sasa Lukic. The 29-year-old could have a medical today at Ipswich where Miami Heat basketball star Udonis Haslem has announced he is a minority owner.

Fulham have failed with a bid for Rennes centre-back Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal.

Ipswich remain in talks with Strasbourg over the signing of Julio Enciso.

Leicester have signed Ipswich winger Wes Burns. The 31-year-old has joined on a three-year deal. Leicester are also in talks for forward Admir Bristric from Olimpija Ljubljana.
