World.title: Tram stop relocation plans criticised by architects' association
World.content:
Tallinn City Government plans to change the locations of tram stops on Pärnu maantee have been criticised by the president of the Association of Architects, who says stops will be placed too far apart.

Deputy mayors Kristjan Järvan (Eesti 200) and Joel Jesse (Center) met with representatives of the Estonian Association of Architects on Thursday to discuss the preliminary design for the reconstruction of Pärnu maantee.

Jesse told ERR the aim is to review the locations of public transport stops to improve transfer opportunities and create more logical stop locations.

He said the Kosmos tram stop will be moved 100 meters toward Liivalaia, next to the intersection.

"The optimal distance between stops is around 600 meters, which means that if you are in the middle, it's a three-minute walk to the next stop. There are also four major schools around the Liivalaia intersection — Tõnismäe Secondary School of Science, the vocational school, Tallinn University of Applied Sciences and the Tallinn School of Music and Ballet," Jesse said.

Joel Jesse. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

At the same time, the walk to the French Lycée would become 100 meters longer.

Jesse said such a solution would allow different modes of public transport to stop together at the same stop more effectively.

However, President of the Estonian Association of Architects Aet Ader said the European practice is for the distance between stops in city centers to be between 200 and 400 meters.

"A distance of more than 600 meters is too long for citizens to choose public transport, especially elderly people, young children and people with mobility impairments," she said.

Ader also said she would like to see more short-term stopping spaces on Pärnu maantee.

Aet Ader Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"It's certainly a welcome idea that there could be more short-term stopping spaces there, but if we look at the current two-plus-two solution — one lane for public transport and one for private cars in each direction. If that were changed to a two-plus-one solution, as they proposed, then yes, short-term stopping spaces could be created. But then private cars, trams and buses would all be using the same lane, and if something happened — a minor collision, an accident, if tram traffic stopped or there were some other incident — there would be no possibility of diverting traffic because there is also a central barrier," Jesse commented.

"We still have to ensure that traffic flows smoothly and safely," he added.

He stressed that there is also a parking garage next to the Rimi supermarket on Pärnu maantee.

But Ader said the city has not presented alternatives to the current 2+2 lane solution.

"In our view, different solutions should be considered, including whether a 2+1 lane solution would be possible. We need to examine in great detail how we could improve the quality of the space so there would be stopping places, businesses could load goods, and taxis or couriers could stop. We also need to consider how to fit a few benches and some greenery into the street corridor to support street life and the functioning of those businesses. I think this should be explored further through more detailed design," Ader said.

Plans for reconstructing a section of Pärnu maantee in Tallinn's city center. Autor/allikas: K-Projekt

She also noted that mistakes could be avoided if, alongside mobility experts, the city also involved spatial planning experts.

"Not enough spatial experts have been involved. We were unable to identify which landscape architect was involved in developing the project to ensure the quality of the public space," the architecture association's president said.

At the same time, Ader acknowledged that the overall project is a step forward because it takes all road users into account.

"But the proposals we have would make it even better. Considering that projects like this are built to last for decades, there are still a few adjustments that could improve it further. Otherwise, it's very positive that the City of Tallinn is tackling this at all. I think Pärnu maantee will also eventually connect with the main street project at Freedom Square. It is one of the capital's most important public spaces," she said.

Jesse said the Pärnu maantee reconstruction project is currently in the design phase, with design work continuing this year and next year, while construction is expected to begin at the end of next year.

"The construction schedule is planned to take approximately two years," he said.

World.title: From gravel roads to handcar rides: Late-summer museum picks across Estonia
World.content:
With summer not yet over, museum expert Kristi Paatsi shares museum and exhibition destinations across Estonia worth adding to your August plans.

August is a great time to explore Estonia's museums, says Kristi Paatsi, a board member of the Estonian Museums Association (EMÜ) ranked one of the world's most influential museum professionals.

With peak tourist season ending, smaller museums in particular can offer quieter visits and often surprisingly personal experiences.

Roadtrip through Saaremaa's past

Can a gravel road be a museum? Absolutely, says Paatsi.

The Lõmala-Kaugatoma Heritage Road on Saaremaa's Sõrve Peninsula acts as an open-air museum, taking visitors back to the 1950s–70s with historic road signs, concrete kilometer markers and other details from the era.

The 11-kilometer route is free to explore by car or bike and invites travelers to slow down, with stops for seaside views or swims, old roadside milk stands and other bits and pieces of rural life. "It's quite the nostalgic trip!" Paatsi said, adding that it's one summer field trip that won't drain your wallet.

A short drive away, the Bulla Museum in Iide village offers another hidden gem. The former home of Carl Oswald Bulla, a world-famous court photographer for the Russian tsar, now showcases his imperial-era photographs from St. Petersburg alongside images of everyday life on the island.

Originally built as a summer home after Bulla married local Saaremaa islander Christine Juliane Keselberg, the house became the couple's permanent residence after the Russian Revolution, allowing the photographer to turn his camera toward island life.

Small museums, big stories

Under the Nõmme pines in Tallinn, the Under and Tuglas Literary Institute offers a glimpse into the lives of Estonian writers Marie Under, Artur Adson, Elo Tuglas and Friedebert Tuglas.

Paatsi recommends visiting on weekdays and leaving time to relax in the garden afterward.

Mõisaküla Museum director Anu Laarmann, also known by the nickname Museum Anu. Source: Arp Müller/ERR

A train ride from the capital brings visitors to Keila, where the Harju County Museum is hosting an exhibition through the end of August on sculptor Amandus Adamson, whose work includes the landmark Russalka Memorial overlooking Tallinn Bay.

Though small in size, Paatsi says the exhibition offers a rare chance to see a surprising number of his works up close.

"If this exhibition were at Kumu, thousands of people would come see it," she said, adding that the smaller, more distant setting makes for an even more special experience.

Southern Estonia's little charms

Just outside Tartu, the Estonian Agricultural Museum (EPM) in Ülenurme, now known as the Rural Curiosity Center (MUHK), is especially worth a visit with the kids.

Alongside regular exhibitions and farm animals including turkeys, quails, rabbits, sheep and ponies, visitors can also currently check out the model-sized Soviet-era collective farm featured in "Look, I Shrank the Kolkhoz!" where tractors, buildings, fields and tools have all been recreated at 1:35 scale.

Heading west toward Viljandi County, the Kapp Family Home Museum in Suure-Jaani introduces visitors to the musical legacy of Estonia's famous Kapp dynasty.

Paatsi said she discovered new details about the Kapp composers herself, including that composer Artur Kapp once raised the blue, black and white flag at his Tallinn home on Estonian Independence Day in 1950 — a bold act during the Soviet occupation under Stalin's rule.

In Mõisaküla, near the Latvian border, the local museum tells the story of the local railway industry, which once produced locomotives, railbuses and carriages, spurring the growth of what is now Estonia's smallest official city.

On sunny days, visitors can even book a handcar ride along the historic tracks.

While both museums are a little worn around the edges, Paatsi said the warmth and enthusiasm of their staff more than make up for it.

"Enjoy summer, go visit museums and explore our cultural history!" she added.

World.title: Universal postal service to slow and prices to rise in fall
World.content:
Letters sent through the universal postal service will be delivered within three business days. Until now, letters could arrive as soon as the next business day. The service will cost €2.10.

Domestic letter delivery prices will rise an average of six percent. Fees for international letters and parcels will increase an average of ten percent.

The content of the universal postal service will also change. The current insured‑item service will be replaced with an optional insurance add‑on that can be purchased for registered mail. Domestic parcels will no longer be part of the universal postal service and will instead be offered as a commercial service.

In addition to Eesti Post, several logistics companies provide this service, and prices are generally lower than the state‑regulated universal postal service rates. Parcels can still be sent and received at post offices, parcel machines or through courier service.

Sigrid Soomlais Source: ERR

Sigrid Soomlais, deputy secretary general for regional development at the Ministry of Regional Affairs and Agriculture, said the ministry wants to adjust the universal postal service to match changing user habits. The goal is also to ensure continued access across Estonia.

"People's daily communication has increasingly moved to digital channels, and the volume of letters sent has declined year after year. At the same time, the universal postal service must remain accessible to everyone nationwide. To do that, the service conditions and fees must be updated so they reflect the actual cost of providing the service as well as people's needs," Soomlais said.

A statement released by the ministry said one out of every three letters last year was sent in December. Nearly 98 percent of letters were sent using a service that assumes delivery within three business days.

In 2025, more than 560,000 letters were sent through the universal postal service, an 18‑percent drop from the previous year. Traditional postal service volume has fallen more than 75 percent over the past five years.

Soomlais said people will still be able to send letters to all regions of Estonia.

Omniva mailbox in Tartu. Source: Airika Harrik/ERR

The Competition Authority submitted the proposal to change universal postal service fees after reviewing the service's cost and the impact of price changes on consumers. The main reasons for updating the price list are higher service‑delivery costs since the last price change, including fuel costs.

Eesti Post will inform customers when the new price list takes effect and provide a detailed schedule.

Eesti Post, which operates under the Omniva brand, is licensed to provide universal postal service as well as domestic and international letter and parcel delivery. The universal postal service provider is selected for five years through a public competition held by the Competition Authority. The current contract runs through 2029.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Iraqi Drilling Company completes well rehabilitation at West Qurna 1 oil field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) has successfully completed the rehabilitation of oil well WQ1-132 at the West Qurna 1 oil field, marking another step in Iraq’s efforts to enhance oil production efficiency and support the long-term development of its energy sector.

The project was carried out as part of the company’s operational program to improve well performance and maintain sustainable crude oil production.

According to a statement issued by the Iraqi Drilling Company, the rehabilitation work was completed in line with directives from Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi and under the supervision of the company’s Director General, Mohammed Hantoosh Asad Al-Azirjawi.

Technical and engineering teams carried out the operation using the company’s specialized expertise and equipment.

The company said the rehabilitation project forms part of its broader strategy to improve the efficiency of existing oil wells while supporting sustainable production across Iraq’s major oil fields.

Restoration work on producing wells helps maximize output, extend operational life, and improve field performance without the need for entirely new drilling operations.

The Iraqi Drilling Company emphasized that the successful completion of the project reflects the capabilities of its engineering and technical staff, who continue to execute specialized rehabilitation operations according to approved operational plans.

The company noted that relying on local expertise strengthens operational efficiency while supporting the continued development of Iraq’s oil infrastructure.

West Qurna 1 is one of Iraq’s largest producing oil fields and plays a significant role in the country’s crude oil output.

Ongoing rehabilitation and maintenance projects are designed to ensure production stability, improve operational reliability, and meet the technical requirements of field development programs.

The completion of well WQ1-132 is expected to contribute to maintaining efficient production operations within the field as Iraq continues investing in the modernization of its energy sector.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Kurdistan president discuss Erbil-Baghdad cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and the president of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Nechirvan Barzani, discussed on Wednesday the country’s political, economic, and security situation.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the two leaders indicated that it is important to boost cooperation between the federal government and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) to enhance stability, address challenges, and serve the interests of the Iraqi people, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi affirmed the government’s commitment to resolving outstanding issues in line with the constitution, preserving Iraq’s unity, and strengthening national partnership.

Barzani stated that it is important to continue dialogue between national parties. He added that the KRG supports the federal government’s efforts to enhance stability and promote national development.

The discussions focused on approaches to secure the success of the government’s national agenda.

This high-level meeting comes after al-Zaidi’s trips to Turkey and Iran, where he met top officials, and Barzani’s visit to Damascus, where he met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

World.title: Iraq wins legal case in Jordan for Samarra Pharmaceutical Company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice has announced a legal victory before the Jordanian judiciary after securing a final court ruling in favor of the State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra, a subsidiary of the Ministry of Industry and Minerals.

The ruling requires a Jordanian company to pay financial compensation following a dispute over the supply of medical materials that failed to meet agreed specifications.

According to a statement from the Ministry of Justice, the ministry’s Legal Department successfully represented the Iraqi pharmaceutical company throughout all stages of the legal proceedings before Jordanian courts.

The case involved a supply contract under which the Jordanian company was expected to provide metal covers for medical supplies. However, the supplier allegedly delivered products that did not comply with the contractual specifications.

Director of the Legal Department, Haitham Mohi Radi, said the final judgment issued by the Jordanian Court of Cassation, and upheld by both the Court of Appeal and the Court of First Instance, ordered the Jordanian company to pay financial amounts to the Samarra-based pharmaceutical company.

The ruling concludes a lengthy legal process aimed at protecting the contractual rights of the Iraqi state-owned enterprise.

The Ministry of Justice described the outcome as an important achievement in safeguarding Iraq’s financial interests abroad.

Officials said the successful litigation reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to defend state institutions before international courts and judicial authorities while protecting public funds from contractual violations.

The ministry added that the case demonstrates the expertise and professionalism of Iraq’s legal teams in handling international commercial disputes.

By successfully pursuing the claim through multiple judicial levels in Jordan, the Legal Department reinforced Iraq’s commitment to enforcing contractual rights and ensuring accountability in cross-border commercial agreements.

The decision is expected to strengthen confidence in the government’s ability to defend the interests of Iraqi public institutions through legal channels.

World.title: Ammar Al-Hakim and Iranian Science Minister discuss academic cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s National State Forces Alliance, Ammar Al-Hakim, met with Iranian Minister of Science, Research and Technology Hossein Simaei Sarraf in Baghdad to discuss expanding academic cooperation between Iraq and Iran through university partnerships, knowledge exchange, and joint educational initiatives.

The meeting focused on strengthening higher education ties while emphasizing the role of universities in addressing labor market needs and societal challenges.

According to a statement released by Al-Hakim’s office, the two sides reviewed opportunities to deepen cooperation between Iraqi and Iranian universities by promoting twinning agreements, expanding academic collaboration, and exchanging expertise.

The discussions highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional relationships to support scientific research and educational development in both countries.

During the meeting, Al-Hakim stressed that university graduates should possess skills that match the demands of today’s job market.

He also urged academic institutions to prioritize scientific research that offers practical solutions to national challenges and contributes to sustainable development.

Al-Hakim emphasized the importance of equipping university students with strong scientific knowledge to prepare them for future professional opportunities.

The Iraqi political leader underscored the role of research institutions in supporting innovation and policymaking.

He noted that universities should focus on producing research capable of addressing economic, social, and developmental issues while enhancing academic excellence.

The discussion reflected a shared interest in strengthening educational cooperation as part of broader bilateral relations.

The meeting also touched on the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage, with Al-Hakim praising the hospitality shown by Iraqis toward visitors traveling to commemorate Imam Hussein.

He said the event demonstrates positive values of solidarity and cooperation, while calling for stronger ties between societies based on shared humanitarian and religious principles.

The visit concluded with discussions on enhancing educational cooperation alongside broader people-to-people engagement between Iraq and Iran.

World.title: Iraq’s State Administration Coalition warns armed groups after September 30
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Administration Coalition has reaffirmed its support for restricting all weapons to state control, warning that any armed activity outside the authority of the government after September 30, 2026, will be treated under the country’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

The position was announced following the coalition’s 37th regular meeting, hosted by Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi, with the participation of Iraq’s senior political and constitutional leaders.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the meeting brought together the President of the Republic, the Speaker of Parliament, the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the Kurdistan Region, and leaders of the State Administration Coalition.

Participants reviewed Iraq’s political, security, economic, and public service developments, as well as regional events and their impact on the country.

The coalition reiterated its backing for the government’s efforts to ensure that all weapons remain under state authority, in line with the government program approved by the Iraqi Parliament.

The coalition stressed that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries or for actions that could draw Iraq into regional conflicts.

It warned that individuals or groups engaging in such activities would be committing crimes that threaten national security.

According to the statement, after September 30, 2026, any armed activity conducted outside the state’s legal framework will be dealt with under Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

Officials also cited constitutional provisions prohibiting the formation of armed organizations outside the official security forces.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi briefed coalition members on government efforts to strengthen security, improve public services, implement the ministerial program, and address Iraq’s financial and economic challenges.

The coalition emphasized the need to:

Maintain national security and stability.

Protect essential public services.

Diversify Iraq’s oil export routes.

Increase non-oil revenues.

Combat corruption, smuggling, and financial waste.

The meeting highlighted the government’s commitment to protecting citizens’ interests while strengthening economic resilience.

On regional affairs, coalition leaders expressed support for diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions across the Middle East.

The meeting reaffirmed Iraq’s rejection of resolving disputes through military force and emphasized Baghdad’s willingness to play a constructive role in promoting dialogue between regional parties.

Participants also discussed border security, counterterrorism cooperation, combating drug trafficking and organized crime, and strengthening relations with neighboring and international partners based on mutual respect and national sovereignty.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the State Administration Coalition called for accelerating the completion of the government formation process and submitting the government’s official program to the Council of Representatives for discussion and approval.

The coalition said completing these constitutional steps remains essential for advancing Iraq’s political stability and governance agenda.

World.title: Any post against PM Modi to be deleted in three hours: Arvind Kejriwal on new social media law
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

supremo

on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Centre over its newly introduced social media law, alleging that it is aimed at silencing criticism of the government and reflects Prime Minister Narendra Modi's growing fear of public protests.

Addressing supporters, former Delhi CM Kejriwal claimed the new law would require social media platforms to take down any post flagged by the government within three hours.

"The Modi government has introduced a new law. If the government asks any social media platform, whether Instagram, Facebook or any other platform, to delete a post or video, it will have to be removed within three hours," he said.

He alleged that the provision would be used to target posts critical of the government on issues such as paper leaks, the ethanol policy and corruption, while allowing abusive content from its supporters to remain online.

"If you speak against Modi ji, the government, paper leaks, the ethanol issue or corruption, your post will be deleted within three hours. But if people associated with them use abusive language or target women, no action is taken against such content," he alleged.

AAP chief Kejriwal further claimed that Prime Minister Modi has become increasingly anxious after recent youth-led protests and demonstrations at Jantar Mantar.





"Modi ji fears the people of this country. He fears the youth, children and women. Ever since the protests at Jantar Mantar, he has been gripped by fear," Kejriwal alleged.

Arguing that censorship cannot substitute governance, the former Delhi chief minister said silencing criticism would only deepen public resentment.

World.title: Govt bars firms filing fake drug data from seeking fresh approvals
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

In a major crackdown on regulatory fraud in the pharmaceutical sector, the Centre has amended the Drugs Rules, 1945 to empower drug regulators to temporarily debar companies that submit fake or fabricated data while seeking approvals for drugs and related licences.

Under the amended rules notified by the Union health ministry on Thursday, applicants found submitting fabricated data will not only face rejection of their applications or cancellation of existing licences, but can also be barred from filing fresh applications before the concerned licensing authority, whether at the Centre or in the states, for a specified period. The action will be taken only after issuing a show-cause notice, and affected applicants will have the right to appeal.

The new provision will apply to all applications filed under the Drugs Rules, 1945, and is aimed at deterring companies from submitting false scientific data to secure regulatory approvals.

The ministry said regulatory decisions on the quality, safety and efficacy of medicines are based on scientific data submitted by applicants. Fabricated data undermines the integrity of the approval process, raises questions about the quality of medicines and can pose serious risks to public health.

World.title: BJP MLAs storm well, disrupt Jharkhand assembly over exam irregularities
World.content:
Opposition BJP MLAs disrupted proceedings of the Jharkhand Assembly over alleged irregularities in a job examination, with several legislators entering the well of the House in protest.

Proceedings of the Jharkhand Assembly were adjourned till 12.30 pm amid an uproar by the BJP MLAs.

During the proceedings, BJP leader Babulal Marandi demanded a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities under a court-monitored panel.

Opposition MLAs raised placards and shouted slogans, including "stop selling students' future" and "recommend a CBI probe into irregularities in JPSC examination", targeting the JMM-led government.

BJP chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleged that the CID probe into the suspected job exam scam had been initiated to "cover up the issues".

"It is an eyewash. The youth doesn't have faith in the CID probe. The protesters will get justice only when a CBI team probes into the irregularities raised by the protesters," Jaiswal said, as cited by PTI.

The protest over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Friday, with six demonstrators continuing their hunger strike.





Meanwhile, two student unions announced plans to march to the state Assembly, which is currently in session, during the day.

The demonstrators have been demanding the cancellation of the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination and an independent probe into the alleged irregularities in the recruitment test, either by the CBI or by a panel of retired High Court judges from outside the state.

World.title: 'Power Banks' for satellites? Bengaluru Company builds tech to keep ageing spacecraft alive
World.content:
BENGALURU: What if satellites could simply plug into a power bank instead of drifting away when they run out of fuel? Thatâs the idea driving a Bengaluru startup building âjetpackâ satellites designed to latch onto ageing spacecraft, take over their propulsion duties and keep billion-dollar assets working years longer.

After recently validating a key part of its technology at an Isro facility used for Indiaâs SpaDeX docking mission, Aule Space is now preparing for what could become one of the worldâs most ambitious private satellite docking demonstrations.

Aule 2: Dark room hardware test setup where the team recreated on-orbit lighting conditions with a sun simulator and a target mounted on a robotic arm to simulate the targetâs motion.

For satellite operators, running out of fuel doesnât necessarily mean spacecraft have reached the end of life. In many cases, expensive communication satellites remain fully functional, but can no longer maintain their assigned orbital positions because they have exhausted the propellant needed for station-keeping.

Once that happens, operators are forced to retire assets worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

Aule has found another way. âWeâre trying to build satellites which can go and dock to existing satellites in space which donât have any installed ports... and extend their life so that they can keep generating revenue,â CEO Jay Panchal, told TOI. âItâs like a power bank,â he added.

Instead of attempting the far more complicated task of refuelling satellites in orbit, Auleâs approach is to send a smaller âjetpackâ spacecraft that docks with an existing communications satellite and assumes responsibility for station-keeping using its own propulsion system.





The company plans to target geostationary communication satellites, many of which cost more than $300 million to build and generate significant annual revenues.

The challenge lies in docking with satellites that were never designed to be serviced. Rather than relying on dedicated docking ports, Aule will attach its spacecraft to the liquid apogee motor (LAM) nozzle, a standard external feature found on most geostationary satellites.

If successful, the technology could help operators extract years of additional service from satellites that would otherwise become orbital relics. Panchal said each docked âjetpackâ could extend a satelliteâs operational life by up to 5 years.

*Key Test Done*

The startup recently completed a major milestone by testing its camera-based guidance, navigation and control system at the Rendezvous Simulation Laboratory (RSL) at Isroâs ISITE â the same lab where critical elements of the SpaDeX were validated.

âWe were the first non-govt entity to access RSL. This is the best kind of on-ground testing we can do for these capabilities,â Panchal said.

One of Auleâs differentiators is its reliance on computer vision instead of multiple specialised sensors. Current docking systems typically use LiDAR, infrared cameras and other sensors. Aule says its spacecraft will perform the critical final approach using a single optical camera powered by onboard AI.

The visual navigation models are trained using data generated in its own facilities and validated at Isroâs testbed before being deployed in orbit.

The company is targeting an in-orbit demonstration next year, when it plans to launch two satellites that will autonomously dock in low-Earth orbit. Panchal claims it could be the worldâs first private mission to perform non-cooperative docking in LEO using camera-only navigation. The mission will validate technologies that Aule ultimately intends to deploy around geostationary communication satellites.

World.title: Jharkhand student protest Day 14: Hunger strike continues as BJP, Rahul Gandhi back students
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday, with students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, while political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified.

The protest, launched on July 25 under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, has grown into one of Jharkhandâs largest student-led movements in recent years. Protesters are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination, an independent probe into alleged irregularities, and comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC. Here are the top developments:

BJP MLAs protest outside Assembly

BJP MLAs on Thursday staged a protest outside the Jharkhand Assembly, on the first day of the Monsoon Session, over alleged irregularities in the state competitive examinations.

Speaking to ANI, BJP MLA Alok Chaurasia said, "The Bharatiya Janata Party stands firmly and vocally with the students regarding the functioning of Jharkhand government agencies such as JPSC, JSSC, and CJL, as well as the widespread corruption across the state, particularly the fraud committed against students..."

The legislators raised slogans against the government, with chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleging it was "selling" Jharkhand's youths' future and demanding a CBI probe, saying, "nobody trusts your CID and committee."





Rahul Gandhi speaks to aspirants

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi spoke to JPSC-JSSC aspirants over the phone on Thursday. Student leader Piyush Kumar said the students raised their demand for cancellation of the examination, an investigation and reforms.

"We told him of our demands, that exam should be cancelled, regarding investigation and reforms. He said that he stands with our demands, and that they will take it up with the Govt. He said that he stands with and supports students...We

are yet to get any official information regarding the date and time of meeting (with the government)," Kumar said.

Student leader Ravindra Paswan said Gandhi enquired about the situation at the protest site.

"He asked us about the situation here. We told him about the irregularities in exams here. We told him that Congress is in the government in Jharkhand and they should help us. He told us that he stands with students," Paswan said.

11-member delegation finalised

According to JPSC JSSC Reform Manch, protesting students have finalised an 11-member delegation for talks with the state government. The group comprises eight student representatives, one lawyer and two technical experts.

The eight student representatives are Piyush Kumar Singh, Ravindra Paswan, Rajesh Prasad, Neetu Kujur, Kartik Soren, Ravindra, Ankit Kumar and Shalu Singh.

Students have also demanded that any dialogue with the government be held in the presence of the media.

Officials reach protest site

Ranchi Sadar SDO Rajat Kumar and ADM Dhananjay Kumar reached Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to hear the grievances of the protesting aspirants.

"We came to speak with our younger brothers about how we can assist them in their preparations for the future," Rajat Kumar said.

A protester said there had been a suggestion that a four- or five-member delegation should participate in talks, but students insisted on a transparent process.

'Assembly gherao' on Monday

Amid the continuing agitation, students announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met. Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision was taken after the government initiated contact with the students.

JMM MLA Jairam Kumar Mahato urged the government to immediately open talks, warning that "something untoward will happen" if the situation remains unresolved.

Hunger strike continues

Activist Sonam Wangchuk rejected reports that student leader Devendra Nath Mahato had ended his hunger strike after speaking with him.

A total of six demonstrators are presently on a hunger strike.

In a video message on X, Wangchuk said, "He consumed water, not food; I want to clarify this."

He added, "He was fasting without water and without food, which is, in a way, like suicide. So, I only urged him to consume water and salt now and continue his fast."

Mahato began his indefinite hunger strike on August 2 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium. He is now continuing the fast on water and salt.

NEW DELHI: The Union ministry of tribal affairs on Thursday told the Lok Sabha that it has received several representations raising concerns over the displacement of people due to the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.The ministry said it has forwarded the representations to the state government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action.In a written reply to questions from Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP Ajendra Singh Lodhi on the rehabilitation of tribal families affected by the project, compliance with the Forest Rights Act (FRA), and alleged evictions, the ministry said it had not received any complaints specifically claiming that compensation disbursed under the project had failed to reach beneficiaries.The ministry, however, said it had received representations "raising issues of displacement" due to the project.It added that the representations had been forwarded to the Madhya Pradesh government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action, while noting that the implementation of the Forest Rights Act (FRA) rests with state governments and Union Territory administrations.Minister of state for tribal affairs Durgadas Uikey, in his written reply, said the representations had been referred to the state authorities. "These have been forwarded to the State Government of Madhya Pradesh and respective District Administrations for examination and necessary action," the reply said.In its response, the ministry said the rehabilitation plan for Scheduled Tribe families affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project was based on a proposal submitted by the National Water Development Agency in 2016.Citing the 2016 proposal, the ministry said the project's first phase is expected to displace 1,913 families comprising 8,339 people, including 648 Scheduled Tribe families.Responding to questions on gram sabha meetings under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), the ministry said it does not maintain centralised records of meeting dates, attendance, signatures, grievances related to consent, compensation and displacement, or the status of their disposal, as implementation of the law falls under the jurisdiction of state governments and Union Territory administrations.The ministry added that it has repeatedly urged states and UTs to ensure that no eligible beneficiary is denied forest rights and to strictly comply with Section 4(5) of the FRA, which prohibits the eviction or removal of claimants from forest land under their occupation until the process of recognition and verification of their rights has been completed.The Centre's response comes amid a prolonged protest by tribal families and other residents affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh's Chhatarpur district over issues related to displacement, rehabilitation and resettlement.As part of the agitation, protesters staged a series of symbolic demonstrations in July, including a "jal satyagraha", "chita (pyre) satyagraha" and "faansi satyagraha".The protest also included an indefinite hunger strike by activist Amit Bhatnagar, who was later forcibly removed from the site by state police. Nearly 150 villagers were also removed during the operation, visuals of which drew nationwide attention.

World.title: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles fast catching up with petrol ones
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles are on the verge of overtaking petrol-powered models in India, with CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles accounting for 40.6% of passenger vehicle retail sales in July, just behind petrolâs 41.7%, according to data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) Thursday.

The gap has narrowed sharply from 13.2 percentage points a year ago to just over a percentage point, reflecting a rapid shift in buyer preferences.

The trend came as Indiaâs automobile retail market recorded its strongest-ever July performance, with overall registrations rising 25.8% year-on-year to a record 25.9 lakh units. For the first time, all six vehicle categories â two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers, tractors and wheeled construction equipment â posted their highest-ever July retail volumes, underscoring broad-based demand across the industry.

Passenger vehicle retail sales increased 19% year-on-year to 4.1 lakh units, crossing the four-lakh mark for the first time in July. Within the segment, CNG vehicles accounted for 24.6% of sales, hybrids for 8% and electric vehicles for 7.9%. While hybrid vehicles continue to use petrol as their primary fuel source, automakers classify them as alternative-fuel vehicles because they combine an internal combustion engine with an electric powertrain to improve efficiency and reduce emissions.





Petrolâs share, meanwhile, declined to 41.6% from 47.6% a year earlier. FADA said fresh model launches, affordability gains following GST changes and consumersâ increasing focus on lower running costs supported demand for alternative powertrains. The dealersâ body also noted that uncertainty surrounding the transition to E20 fuel appears to have nudged some buyers towards CNG, hybrid and EVs.

World.title: Telangana physiotherapy student secures job in Germany through TOMCOM
World.content:
A physiotherapist from the State found employment in Germany with a starting monthly salary of ₹3.5 lakh after completing German language training, Telangana Overseas Manpower Company said in a statement

P. Aishwaryarani contacted TOMCOM to find employment. As a next step, she took a course in German language and completed its B2. Thus, achieving a requirement for placement in Germany’s healthcare sector.

Labour, Employment, Training & Factories and Mines and Geology Minister G Vivek Venkatswamy handed over her appointment letter and congratulated her.

Mr Vivek said that the Telangana government was committed to creating overseas employment opportunities by equipping youth with skills and foreign language proficiency. He said TOMCOM was helping prepare young professionals for global careers through skill development, language training and placement support.

Ms Aishwaryarani’s remuneration is expected to increase after completing the mandatory professional training and certification requirements. Director of Employment and Training Kanthi Wesley also congratulated her and encouraged Telangana youth to utilise TOMCOM’s training programmes.

World.title: ‘When government does not control masjids and churches, why have control over temples?’
World.content:
The Vishwa Hindu Parishad will shortly launch a massive campaign to free temples from government control, said VHP international president Alok Kumar in Mangaluru on Thursday.

Speaking to reporters at the VHP office, Mr. Kumar said the campaign was aimed at bringing temples back under the control of devotees and Hindu society.

“When the government does not exercise control over masjids and churches, why should it have a hold over ₹1,000 crore in income from temples? The income that the Karnataka government gets from the Kukke Subrahmanya temple is the highest it receives from temples in the state. If temples in the country come under the control of Hindu society, this revenue can be used for Hindu society’s religious and educational activities,” he said.

As part of the campaign, the VHP will meet Chief Ministers, Governors, elected representatives, religious heads, and the public, holding conventions in support of the initiative. The Mandir Mukti Abhiyan will be as successful as the VHP’s Rama Janmabhoomi, uniform civil code, and anti-cow slaughter campaigns, he said.

“The entire Hindu community is hurt by the enactment of the ‘Chanda Chori’ skit in front of Parliament, in which sadhus were wrongly projected as ‘chanda choors’. None of the sadhus has been named as an accused in the Ayodhya Ram Temple hundi theft case. Despite this, Rahul Gandhi, Pappu Yadav, and other opposition leaders have maligned ‘Sanatana Dharma’ by enacting the skit. Devotees will definitely give a befitting reply in the forthcoming elections,” Mr. Kumar added.

He said the ongoing investigation into the hundi theft issue was likely to be completed shortly, and by the end of this year, the accused would be sentenced to harsh imprisonment. He expressed confidence that the temple management would take steps to prevent such incidents in the future and regain the trust of devotees, adding that the issue had been unnecessarily politicised.

‘No need to react’

Referring to a letter from Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge seeking the accounts of the RSS, Mr. Kumar said: “The RSS does not need to react to the letter. He has no authority to ask for it.” Courts have held that ‘guru dakshina’ from shakhas to the RSS is not an income, and hence no income tax can be levied. “Just for his own popularity, the Minister has written a letter,” Mr. Kumar said.

While agreeing with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s stand to pardon agitators at Jantar Mantar who raised their voice over the NEET paper leak, Mr. Kumar expressed concern over vulgar comments made by some agitators and the way they attacked policemen in New Delhi.

World.title: CBI files chargesheet against 11 accused in killing of Suvendu’s aide
World.content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) filed a chargesheet on Thursday (August 6, 2026) against 11 accused in the murder of West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari’s personal assistant, Chandranath Rath.

Two brothers were arrested in relation to the crime and were named as accused in the case.

The two brothers, Sagar Sonkar and Sahib Sonkar, residents of north Kolkata were arrested on August 1 for close links with the assassins, officials said. They said that Sagar had previously worked with Rath and was one of the key conspirators who helped in conspiring the murder.

The central agency is also investigating links of the murder with a rival political party after call records allegedly showed repeated calls with a local party office. CBI officials have also said that the conspiracy may have been in the works since December 2025 and was well planned out.

One of the accused, Sagar had reportedly ordered the contract killing of Rath and hired the trained assassins from Uttar Pradesh for the job. During investigation it has also been learnt that Sagar had previously worked with a rival political party, before shifting to the Bharatiya Janta Party.

On May 6, two days after the BJP won the elections for the first time in West Bengal, Rath was gunned down in a moving vehicle by bike-borne assassins on the outskirts of Kolkata in the Madhyamgram area. He was hit by bullets at a point blank range and collapsed on the spot. Massive attention was drawn to this high-profile murder as three accused were arrested from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar as political mud-slinging continued.

Till now officials have arrested contract killers — Monu Singh, Raj Singh, Golu Singh, Mayank Raj Mishra, Vickey Maurya, and Naveen Kumar Singh. They have also arrested middlemen Vinay Rai, Sanjay Rai, and Vikas Mishra. One of the accused remains absconding, according to officials.

The CBI took over the investigation on May 12 as Uttar Pradesh Congress claimed that one of the arrested accused has close links to the BJP.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 15 updates: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026’ passed in Lok Sabha without debate
World.content:
The Lok Sabha on Friday (August 7, 2026) passed The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026. The Bill, which replaces the 2006 Act, provides for the notification of a national digital platform for the free and voluntary registration of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Both Houses of Parliament were adjourned till 11 a.m. on August 10.

Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, on Friday reiterated his demand for the Union Home Minister Amit Shah to deliver a statement on police action against protestors on July 20. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju told the protesting Opposition members in the Lok Sabha that, Opposition can not decide when a Minister would attend the House. Mr. Kharge, claimed that the Chairperson, C.P. Radhakrishnan, had issued a direction to Mr. Shah; however, Mr. Rijiju refuted the claim. Mr. Rijiju said that that RS Chairman did not give direction to any Minister to be present in the House.

“I think he (Union Home Minister Amit Shah) is afraid to come (to Parliament). He is not coming for some reason. He should come, he should answer, and he should make a statement. What is the big deal in that? If something wrong has happened, then take responsibility”, said Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.

World.title: SWR cancels day trains on Bengaluru-Mangaluru sector in October
World.content:
The South Western Railway has decided to cancel day train services on the Bengaluru-Mangaluru/Karwar sector for a month in October to provide line block for tamping work and material train movement on the Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya Road Ghat section.

However, the services would be operated during the Navarathri/ Dasara holidays so as to not inconvenience holiday travellers. The cancelled services include Train No. 16515/516 Yeshwantpur-Karwar-Yeshwantpur tri-weekly, Train No. 16575/576 Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru Junction-Mangaluru Junction Gomateshwara tri-weekly and Train No. 16539/540 Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru Junction-Mangaluru Junction weekly express services.

Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd., (KRCL) and Southern Railway have said Train No. 16575 Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru Junction Gomateshwara Express remains cancelled on October 4, 6, 8, 11, 13, 15, 22, 25, 27, 29, November 1 and 3. Train No. 16576 Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur Gomateshwara Express remains cancelled on October 5, 7, 9, 12, 14, 16, 23, 26, 28, 30, November 2 and 4.

Train No. 16515 Yeshwantpur-Karwar Express would be cancelled on October 5, 7, 9, 12, 14, 21, 23, 26, 28, 30 and November 2. Train No. 16516 Karwar-Yeshwantpur Express would be cancelled on October 6, 8, 10, 13, 15, 22, 24, 27, 29, 31 and November 3. Train No. 16539 Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru Junction weekly Express remains cancelled on October 10, 24 and 31 while Train No. 16540 Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur weekly Express would be cancelled on October 11, 25 and November 1.

Long overdue

Divisional Railway Manager of Mysuru Division Mudit Mittal, in whose jurisdiction the line block is effected, told The Hindu that the ballast tamping work was long overdue between Yadakumari-Siribagilu stations on the Ghat section, where landslip too had occurred recently.

“This was the least amount of time required for tamping and other works,” he said when asked about the very long duration of cancellation. Further, services would be operated during the Navaratri/ Dasara holidays, he noted.

Ballast have become uneven in the section requiring movement of the Multi-purpose Tamper Machine every day. Progress of tamping would be very slow.

The Railways waited till the closure of advance reservation window to cancel the services, thereby minimising inconvenience to travellers, the DRM added.

Six months cancelled

The SWR had cancelled the day train services from June to December 15, 2025, to facilitate Railway Electrification work on this Ghat section.

World.title: Tamil Nadu govt. defends State’s power to provide quota to Muslim converts from backward classes, SC to decide
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (August 7, 2026) agreed to pronounce judgment on a Tamil Nadu government appeal seeking confirmation of the State’s power to frame and implement policy to provide reservation benefits to members of backward classes, most backward classes, denotified communities and Scheduled Castes who convert to Islam.

A Bench headed by Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra reserved orders on the State government’s stand that it has the authority, based on the Tamil Nadu Backward Classes Commission, to issue “backward classes (Muslim) community certificates to eligible persons who had embraced Islam among the backward classes, most backward classes, denotified communities and Scheduled Castes”.

The State, represented by senior advocates Mukul Rohatgi and Siddharth Luthra, said the object behind its government order of March 9, 2024 was to ensure that “persons belonging to socially and educationally backward communities are not deprived of reservation benefits solely on account of conversion to Islam and thereby create a level playing field by preserving affirmative action benefits despite change of religion”.

The State appeal was directed against a Madras High Court decision quashing the March 2024 order as unconstitutional.

The High Court judgment of June 25 had held that “a person who embraces Islam cannot claim the status of backward class(Muslim)”.

Justice Mishra orally observed that a 1951 judgment of the Madras High Court in G. Michael versus S. Venkateswaran, regarding a Scheduled Caste member who converted to Christianity and wanted to contest in a reserved seat, had held the fort for 75 years by upholding the constitutional validity of Paragraph 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.

Paragraph 3 stipulated that no person who professed a religion different from Hinduism (later amended to include Sikhism and Buddhism) should be deemed to get the benefits of a Scheduled Caste member.

The State however contended that the 1951 judgment did not disable the State from classifying a convert who was previously socially and educationally backward as a backward Muslim under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) of the Constitution.

It said the March 24 order applied to the “wholly distinct category of backward class notification, which contains no religion-based exclusion”.

The court was hearing the petition filed by a man from Thoothukudi district who had embraced Islam and changed his name. He was born to Hindu parents. The certificate issued by the Sunnath Jamath, Kayathar, in 2015 had stated the petitioner had embraced Islam.

He had applied for a community certificate certifying him as ‘Muslim Lebbai’, a faith he claimed to follow. However, the Kayathar Tahsildar rejected his application. Challenging it, he had moved court.

Meanwhile, the 2024 government order was notified, working in his favour.

But the High Court had held that a Hindu, on conversion to Islam, did not carry forward the benefits of the Hindu caste or sub-caste. The convert’s status in Islam was not decided by the caste he was part of prior to the conversion.

The High Court had noted that Christian missionaries as well as Islamic preachers maintained that their religions offered social equality unlike Hinduism, which had a caste hierarchy.

“Having taken such a stand for effecting conversions, it is disingenuous to claim that there is hierarchy in Islam also. In our respectful view, categorising certain sects as Backward and the remaining as Forward is antithetical to Quranic injunctions. Islam seeks to establish an egalitarian society. Everyone is equal in the eye of God. There is no social hierarchy,” the High Court had reasoned.

World.title: Bengal BJP fights against its ‘Trinamoolification’
World.content:
Days after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) swept the West Bengal Assembly poll in 2026, winning 207 of the 293 seats, West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya made a bold political claim. “Our doors are closed for Trinamool. There will be no ‘Trinamoolification’ of the BJP,” Mr. Bhattacharya had said. The 62-year-old leader, who had been a foot soldier of the party when its vote share was in single digits in West Bengal was among the first to use the phrase, ‘Trinamoolification of the BJP’.

He didn’t know then that on the afternoon of July 9, he would be handing out lotus-insignia party flags to three former Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs at the BJP office in Kolkata’s Salt Lake area. The three MPs were Sukhendu Sekhar Ray, Sushmita Dev, and Prakash Chik Baraik. They had been nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the Trinamool Congress, and had resigned after the party suffered an electoral setback in the Assembly poll. When in the Trinamool, they had publicly criticised the BJP.

Within hours of Mr. Bhattacharya welcoming the Trinamool leaders into the BJP fold, the party announced that the former Trinamool MPs were to be renominated to the Upper House with the support of newly elected BJP legislators. Mr. Bhattacharya tried to defend opening doors for the Trinamool leaders by saying that the decision was in national interest.

“Syama Prasad Mookerjee has taught us that the party is bigger than an individual, and the nation is bigger than the party,” he said, trying hard to say that inducting the three leaders into the party was an “exception”.

The Bengal BJP president who had spoken about the party’s doors being closed for Trinamool members, is now saying that those in the Trinamool who could not raise their voices in the party are now knocking on BJP doors and the party may consider opening its doors at an opportune moment.

Feeling the heat of the Trinamoolification

A month after this incident, Mr. Bhattacharya admits that the anger among the BJP rank and file was so much that those supporters who were singing his praises during the election are putting a garland of shoes around his photograph. “Usually the garland is made of old shoes, but I saw that the shoes were all new,” the BJP leader quipped. Several BJP leaders, such as State Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta, said they found it difficult to participate in the flag handing-over event.

To many, the Trinamoolification of the BJP started even before the party won the 2026 Assembly poll. Former West Bengal BJP president Dilip Ghosh, now a prominent Minister in the West Bengal government, took a swipe at Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari by saying that it was not new for Trinamool leaders to join the BJP. “Where is it written in the BJP that people from other parties cannot join. Our Chief Minister is also a former Trinamool (leader),” Mr. Ghosh said.

Mr. Ghosh’s reference to Mr. Adhikari points to the unease in BJP’s rank and file. Mr. Adhikari, once a key Trinamool leader and Minister in Mamata Banerjee’s government, defected to the BJP in December 2020. Mr. Adhikari, who defeated Mamata Banerjee twice at Nandigram in 2021 and Bhabanipur in 2026, was chosen to lead the BJP government in West Bengal, five years after joining the party.

Good TMC vs not-so-good TMC

After the defeat in the West Bengal Assembly poll in 2026, the Trinamool Congress has been torn apart by rebellion and desertions. The majority of Lok Sabha MPs and party MLAs decided to part ways with party chairperson Mamata Banerjee.

Despite being the beneficiaries of the Trinamool Congress’s politics, these MPs and MLAs have blamed the party chairperson for favouring her nephew Abhishek Banerjee and allowing corruption and misrule to persist.

Of the 28 Lok Sabha MPs of the Trinamool Congress, 20 have merged with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), and have become a part of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA).

Of the 80 MLAs of the Trinamool Congress who were elected to the 18th West Bengal Legislative Assembly, 65 legislators decided to support the claim of Ritabrata Banerjee as the Leader of the Opposition, against the writ of Mamata Banerjee. One of the reasons behind the rebellion of both the MPs and MLAs of the Trinamool Congress is the opportunity to cosy up to the BJP, the party in power both at the Centre and in the State.

The BJP leadership in West Bengal, which is perceived as being soft on the rebel MPs and MLAs, has come out with a theory of “bhalo (good) Trinamool”. The Lok Sabha MPs, who have decided to join the NDA, have allegedly been told that after delimitation, when the seats increase, so will their chances of returning to Parliament in 2029.

On August 4, Chief Minister Adhikari met the NCPI MPs in Delhi. He was joined by Union Minister Bhupender Yadav, who was election-in-charge of West Bengal, and BJP MP Nishikant Dubey. If the photograph of Samik Bhattacharya handing over party flags to the three Rajya Sabha MPs created discomfort in the BJP’s rank and file, the Chief Minister’s photograph with the NCPI MPs was reason for heartburn.

The “good Trinamool” is the rebel camp led by Leader of the Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee. Mr. Banerjee, who was a Communist Party of India (Marxist) nominee to Rajya Sabha, joined the Trinamool Congress in 2020 after the CPI(M) expelled him. The Trinamool Congress re-nominated him to Rajya Sabha for a second term in 2024. In 2026, he resigned from the Upper House to contest the Assembly poll from Uluberia Purba.

The rebel MLAs led by his camp are claiming to be the “original Trinamool” and have sought the party’s symbol from the Election Commission and laid claim to hundreds of crores of party funds.

After the change of regime, hundreds of local-level Trinamool Congress workers have been arrested by the police on charges of corruption, extortion, and electoral violence. Many were attacked with eggs when they were being taken into custody or being produced before courts. However, the MPs and MLAs of the “good Trinamool” have not faced police action after warming up to the BJP.

Among the handful of loyalists left by Mamata Banerjee’s side is Beleghata MLA Kunal Ghosh. After an under-construction warehouse collapsed in Kolkata’s Taratala area on June 24 burying 16 workers, Chief Minister Adhikari blamed it on the former Trinamool Congress regime.

Mr. Adhikari held up a document in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly with the signature of former mayor of Kolkata Municipal Corporation Firhad Hakim, and said no one would be spared. Ghosh dared the Chief Minister to act against Hakim to prove that the State government was serious about taking action against those responsible for the deaths. Hakim, who was one of the key Ministers during Mamata Banerjee’s regime, joined the Ritabrata Banerjee camp, and despite the Chief Minister blaming him for the tragedy, the only high-profile arrest was his former personal assistant.

The reverse ‘egg therapy’

With the majority of the Trinamool leaders now part of the “good Trinamool” camp, it is Mamata Banerjee and a handful of her loyalists who are being blamed by the BJP for they say was “misrule and corruption” over the past 15 years. The BJP government in West Bengal is yet to complete 100 days. It is already faced with something it had accused the Trinamool Congress leadership of over the past several years: extortion and political corruption.

In the past three months several businesses have alleged that BJP leaders have demanded money from them and they have had to reach out to the police seeking protection.

Sources in the BJP said that the party has suspended 22 functionaries, including several mandal presidents, over allegations of extortion and indiscipline.

Senior leaders of the BJP, including party president are warning its workers against extortion. While former State BJP president and Minister Dilip Ghosh said that many leaders are becoming addicted to this “honey of extortion”, the current State BJP chief has warned party members to mend their ways.

“The unwarranted egg therapy we see now (referring to Trinamool leaders being attacked with eggs) can turn on its head and start falling on the other side as well. Everyone, including those in my party, must understand that. Those ‘Sanatanis’ who have suddenly found a place in our party and are harbouring aspirations for influence and advantage must also remain careful because the trajectory of those eggs can change in no time,” Bhattacharya said.

It is the BJP workers in the districts who are most upset with Trinamool leaders warming up to the BJP, but only a few have mustered the courage to speak about it publicly. Nikhil Ranjan Dey, a former BJP MLA from Cooch Behar, came out in public against the nomination of the three former Trinamool Congress MPs to Rajya Sabha by his party.

“We do not know what our central leadership is thinking. They want to increase numbers in Parliament. But why will (former) Trinamool leaders be nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the BJP? Are there not enough qualified and educated people in the BJP?” the former MLA said.

Mr. Dey said that several BJP workers have suffered at the hands of the Trinamool Congress and are still languishing behind the bars after being booked under what he claims are false charges during the Trinamool Congress regime.

In fact, former Trinamool leaders had once even allegedly called for violence against BJP members. One such example is of former Trinamool Congress MP and actor Nushrat Jahan, who represented the Jadavpur Lok Sabha seat from 2019 to 2024.

She was photographed with BJP leaders at an event to honour exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasrin. The photo went viral and was criticised by several right-wing online portals.

The portals highlighted how, before the election, the actor-turned-politician had been heard telling the electorate to beat up BJP leaders with bamboo sticks if they came seeking votes.

Personal versus the political

Sudip Bandyopadhay is an MP from the Kolkata North Lok Sabha seat. After parting ways with Mamata Banerjee, he is the senior-most MP of the NCPI, and is now holding meetings with the BJP leadership in the national capital.

While Mr. Bandyopadhay is meeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Adhikari, BJP’s Tapas Roy, now Minister of Industries and Commerce in the West Bengal government, is fuming. “I will never have anything to do with him. I hate him, because of what he did to me,” Mr. Roy said.

The Manicktala MLA left the Trinamool Congress and joined the BJP in 2024. That year, he lost the Lok Sabha polls to Mr. Bandyopadhay. Mr. Roy has publicly said that Mr. Bandyopadhay was the reason he had to quit the Trinamool Congress, and join the BJP. He claims that Mr. Bandyopadhay was behind a raid at his residence when he was with the Trinamool, a charge Mr. Bandyopadhay has vehemently denied.

The only thing that is keeping the 70-year-old BJP leader happy: “It is very comforting to see the Trinamool Congress crumbling.”
